s: 面向用户 · 开始使用
b: Gitoodo 是 AI 编程智能体的编排器。工作写在你代码托管平台上的议题里：你可以自己编写，也可以在对话中描述目标，让它为你创建。Gitoodo 把它们分派给智能体，智能体交付拉取请求。 代码托管平台始终是唯一的事实来源：标签、评论和拉取请求随时显示谁在做什么。只有当问题、审批或故障在等你时，你才需要介入。 议题的产生：你可以在 Forge 上或在仓库视图中用 新任务 自己编写，也可以让 对话 根据你的目标起草，并在你确认后创建。worker 也可以为其议题之外的工作提议后续议题；它会直接进入队列，除非仓库要求你先批准。 分类器检查它并标记为就绪。 调度器启动一个智能体。它在自己的工作副本中工作，并打开一个拉取请求。 所有检查通过后，Gitoodo 合并拉取请求并关闭议题。 仅“问我的” 没有编排器时（直接模式，商店版本也是如此），Gitoodo 只是 问我的 列表：显示你所有仓库和账户中等你处理的事项，并提供计数和通知。在 设置 的 编排 中切换模式。 应用中“帮助与反馈 → 帮助中心”里有相同的文字。

s: 面向用户 · 开始使用
b: Gitoodo 是你仓库的编排器：你描述想要构建什么，Gitoodo 把它变成议题，并让编程智能体（Claude Code、Codex 或 Gemini CLI）作为 工作进程 来处理，直到拉取请求被合并。每个仓库都是一个工作场所：侧边栏在它下面列出正在运行的会话，它的视图以磁贴显示这些会话，一个开关即可开启或暂停自动驾驶。没有编排器时只保留 问我的 ：Gitoodo 会收集所有等你处理的事项。本页带你从安装一直走到第一个工作进程。 你需要什么 一台搭载 Apple 芯片的 Mac，或 Windows 10/11（x64）。 Forgejo、Gitea、GitHub 或 GitLab 上的账户，自托管的也可以。 使用编排器时：一个你已在用并已登录的智能体命令行工具（Claude Code、Codex 或 Gemini CLI）。工作进程使用你自己的订阅运行；Gitoodo 不需要 API 密钥。 安装 macOS（Apple 芯片）。 在终端中运行一行命令，会下载已签名并经过公证的发布版本，校验其 SHA-256，把 Gitoodo 安装到 /Applications （或 ~/Applications ），把 gitoodo 命令链接到 ~/.local/bin ，并打开应用。再次运行即可原地更新；不需要 sudo。 curl -fsSL https://gitoodo.com/install.sh | bash 要彻底移除 Gitoodo（应用、命令、服务、设置、缓存、日志、已保存的令牌、智能体技能和隐私权限）： curl -fsSL https://gitoodo.com/uninstall.sh | bash 在删除 Gitoodo 克隆的仓库之前它会先询问，并且绝不会动你自己的检出目录； --dry-run 只显示它会删除什么。 Windows 10/11（x64）。 在 PowerShell 中运行一行命令，会读取发布信息，校验安装程序的 SHA-256 及其发布者（代码签名），仅为你的用户把 Gitoodo 安装到 %LOCALAPPDATA%\Gitoodo ，把 gitoodo 命令加入你的 PATH，并打开应用。再次运行即可原地更新；不需要管理员权限。 irm https://gitoodo.com/install.ps1 | iex 如果某个版本的 Windows 安装程序尚未签名，该命令会在安装任何内容之前停止并说明原因；请改为从下载区下载安装程序 .exe 。Windows SmartScreen 随后会警告发布者未知：选择 更多信息 ，再选择 仍要运行 。 要彻底移除 Gitoodo（应用、命令、后台任务、设置、缓存、日志、凭据管理器中已保存的令牌、开机自启和智能体技能）： irm https://gitoodo.com/uninstall.ps1 | iex 与 macOS 一样，在删除 Gitoodo 克隆的仓库之前它会先询问，并且绝不会动你自己的检出目录。选项写在脚本之后，例如 & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://gitoodo.com/uninstall.ps1))) -DryRun 。你也可以从项目的 Releases 页面下载安装程序 .exe 并运行；在批准系统提示之前，请先核对发布者。 从源码构建。 安装好 Rust、Node.js 和 Tauri 2 的前置条件后，运行 npm ci 和 npm run tauri build 即可为当前系统构建安装程序；参见 构建 。 引导 首次启动时，Gitoodo 会带你完成一个简短的引导。每一步都可以跳过，之后可以在 帮助与反馈 → 入门 中重新进行整个引导。 语言。 Gitoodo 跟随系统语言；可在“设置 → 通用”中更改。 Gitoodo 应如何工作？ 选择 编排器 （推荐）或 直接 。可随时在“设置 → 模式”中切换。 连接你的代码托管平台。 输入服务器地址和令牌。令牌助手会询问 Gitoodo 应该对你的仓库做什么（根据你刚选的模式预先选中），打开你所用平台的令牌页面，并在一个区块中列出令牌为此所需的全部权限，附上原因以及你的账户需要的角色。确认你已设置这些权限后，粘贴令牌并点击 检查 。令牌会进入系统密钥存储（macOS 钥匙串、Windows 凭据管理器），绝不会写入文件或日志。 仓库。 打开你希望 Gitoodo 读取的仓库。关闭的仓库完全不会被查询。 设置编排器 （仅编排器模式）。Gitoodo 会用同样的方式设置你刚选中的每个仓库：标签、开启以及本地副本，另外还有后台服务、技能和调度器。 通知。 允许通知，这样即使窗口关闭，Gitoodo 也能在有决定等你时提醒你。点击通知会打开它所涉及的内容：问题、所在仓库中的 issue、工作机或状态页。 启动与快捷键。 决定 Gitoodo 是否在登录时启动，以及用哪个键盘快捷键从任意应用中打开它。 使用统计。 最后一步会显示匿名使用统计及其发送的内容；你可以在这里将其关闭。完成引导之前不会发送任何内容。 之后 Gitoodo 会以一个对勾的形式常驻在 macOS 菜单栏或 Windows 通知区域。对勾变红时，表示有事项在等你。 先说编排器模式 如果你选择了编排器，引导会以 设置助手 结束。它会立即检查设置的每个部分，并补上缺少的内容： 后台服务（ gitoodo service install ：launchd、systemd 用户单元或计划任务）， 每个仓库中的状态标签， 为编排开启该仓库以及本地工作副本， 智能体说明和可选的 gitoodo-questions 技能， 启动工作进程的调度器，以及检查你的智能体命令行工具是否已安装并已登录。 你可以在“设置 → 模式”中点击 开始设置 再次打开助手；每一步也都可以手动完成，参见 编排器设置 。 之后的工作流程是这样的： 用任一方式把议题放进仓库：在 对话 标签页描述你的计划，编排器会建议仓库和议题，并且只有在你点击之后才创建；或者自己写议题，在代码托管平台上写，或在仓库视图中用 新任务 。Gitoodo 对两者一视同仁。 调度器为每个就绪的议题启动一个工作进程，各自在独立的 worktree 和分支中运行。每个工作进程作为一个会话运行：显示在侧边栏中它所属的仓库下面，以及该仓库视图中的一个磁贴。点击磁贴可将其放大；在这里你可以接管、向智能体发送指令、暂停、继续、取消或重启。在每个视图中，标题栏都会告诉你一切是否正常运行，或有多少事项需要你处理。 工作进程需要做决定时，会在它的议题中提问。问题会在 问我的 中显示为一张回答卡片，并预先选中推荐项。 完成的拉取请求会按你的仓库允许的方式合并；参见 合并与发布 。 Mac App Store 的商店版没有编排器：它的沙盒不允许后台服务和工作进程。编排器随直接下载的版本提供。 只有“问我的”（直接模式） 直接模式只需要一个账户。Gitoodo 会在应用中轮询你的代码托管平台，并显示跨仓库、跨账户等你处理的事项：议题中的问题、分配给你的议题、评审请求和状态标签，同时提供托盘计数和通知。它不会启动工作进程，也不会改动标签。两种模式读取的是同样的议题，所以你可以先用直接模式，以后再在“设置 → 模式”中切换到编排器。 下一步 日常使用 ：四个标签页，以及使用 Gitoodo 的一天是什么样。 问题 ：智能体如何提问，你如何回答。 设置 ：所有设置集中在一处。 如果有什么不起作用，请看 故障排除 和 常见问题 。

t: 在自托管的 Forgejo 或 Gitea 上使用编程智能体
h: 为什么适合自托管的代码托管平台
为什么适合自托管的代码托管平台
只允许快进合并的仓库

b: Gitoodo 把你自己的 Forgejo 或 Gitea 服务器上的议题变成编程智能体的工作：每个就绪的议题一个工作进程，最后产出一个拉取请求，并以你的仓库允许的方式合并。本指南带你从服务器地址一直走到第一个已合并的拉取请求，并说明自动驾驶需要哪些分支规则。 为什么适合自托管的代码托管平台 Forgejo 和 Gitea 与 GitHub 和 GitLab 一样受到支持，可以是任意地址，也可以与其他代码托管平台上的账户并存。 中间没有 Gitoodo 服务器：应用及其后台服务直接从你的电脑与你的代码托管平台通信。Gitoodo 会联系哪些地址以及原因，列在 网络清单 （英文）中。 工作进程运行你已在用并已登录的智能体命令行工具（Claude Code、Codex 或 Gemini CLI），使用你自己的订阅。Gitoodo 不需要 API 密钥。 令牌只保存在系统密钥存储中，绝不会写入文件或日志。 1. 连接你的账户 按照 入门 中的说明安装 Gitoodo，并在引导中选择 编排器 。然后输入服务器地址和令牌。Forgejo 和 Gitea 无法通过链接预先选好令牌权限，因此令牌助手会打开你服务器上的令牌页面，并列出每一项权限及其访问级别和原因。设置好这些权限后，粘贴令牌并点击 检查 。按模式列出的完整权限见 代码托管平台令牌 （英文）。 设置会推荐使用一个单独的 工作进程账户 ，这样代码托管平台上的历史记录显示的是它的名字，而不是你的。如果你的账户是站点管理员，在你确认一份摘要后，Gitoodo 可以替你创建它：一个受限账户，只对你开启的那些仓库拥有写权限，以及一个只带工作进程所需权限的令牌。你也可以继续使用自己的账户。详情见 编排器设置 （英文）。 2. 选择仓库和标签 开启 Gitoodo 应该在其中工作的仓库；所有仓库一开始都是关闭的。在写入任何内容之前，Gitoodo 会为每个仓库显示它将保留、重命名或创建哪些标签。它绝不会删除标签。从此以后，标签记录每个议题的状态： ready 、 in-progress 、 in-review 、 needs-human ，以及 标签 中介绍的其他标签。 你还要决定如何处理已经打开的议题：只处理新议题，把现有议题视为就绪，或者先检查它们并询问你。 3. 本地副本 每个工作进程都在本地副本的独立 worktree 中工作。缺少副本时，Gitoodo 会用已连接的账户把它克隆到自己的克隆文件夹（默认为 ~/gitoodo/repos ），因此即使是私有仓库，电脑上也既不需要 SSH 密钥，也不需要 git 凭据助手。如果仓库已经在你的某个文件夹中，就让设置指向那里：Gitoodo 随后只会拉取并添加它自己的 gitoodo/… 分支和 worktree，绝不会检出、重置或清理你的工作树。 4. 开启自动驾驶 设置会安装后台服务并开启自动驾驶。从此以后，当你信任的人写了一个描述完整的议题，或者议题带有 ready 标签时，它就会变为就绪；其他任何人的议题会先收到一个批准问题。调度器为每个就绪的议题在独立的分支中启动一个工作进程，例如 gitoodo/42-login-fix 。侧边栏中仓库所在行的开关可以再次暂停自动驾驶。 5. 合并所需的分支规则 Gitoodo 使用合并账户进行合并：即工作进程账户，如果没有，则是你自己的账户。在 Forgejo 或 Gitea 中打开 设置 → 分支 ，再打开你的目标分支的规则： 合并白名单： 如果启用，合并账户必须在名单上。Gitoodo 中的 允许合并账户 会把它加进去；这需要你对该仓库拥有管理员权限。 状态检查： 列出的检查必须与你的 CI 在拉取请求上实际报告的检查一致。一个被重命名的检查会阻止所有合并。 所需批准： 这样每个拉取请求都会等待人来批准。Gitoodo 绝不会批准它自己的工作。 分支过时时阻止合并： 没问题，Gitoodo 会自己把分支更新到最新。 你开启一个仓库时，Gitoodo 会立即读取这条规则，并指出任何会让自动驾驶停下的问题，同时给出解决它的操作。更多内容见 分支规则 （英文）。 只允许快进合并的仓库 有些自托管的仓库只允许快进合并。Gitoodo 使用你的仓库允许的方式；如果所选方式不被允许，就按 squash、仅快进、合并提交、rebase 的顺序取第一个允许的方式。在仅快进的情况下，它会把落后的工作进程分支变基到目标分支上，再次等待检查，然后合并的正是经过检查的那个提交。真正的冲突绝不会被强行处理：拉取请求会收到一条列出相关文件的评论，议题则等你处理。 先设置好 CI 如果没有任何检查，Gitoodo 会等待三分钟看是否出现检查，然后合并。所以请为仓库配一个由你的分支规则设为必需的 CI 任务，例如使用 Forgejo Actions 或 Gitea Actions。设置中的 设置项目 可以添加一个入门用的门禁工作流，你再往里填入真正的检查。合并前还必须满足哪些条件，见 安全的自动合并 。 开始使用 下载 Gitoodo ，然后按照 入门 从安装一直走到第一个工作进程。

t: 让编程智能体自动处理 GitHub 议题
b: 有了 Gitoodo，一个就绪的 GitHub 议题无需你启动会话就能变成已合并的拉取请求：一个工作进程接手议题并创建拉取请求，等你的仓库要求的检查通过后，调度器就会合并它。本页展示其中每一步，以及你只需设置一次的内容。GitLab 上的流程相同，只是用合并请求。 你需要什么 一个 GitHub 账户和一个令牌。令牌助手会打开 GitHub 的经典令牌页面并预先选好权限，同时解释每一项；细粒度令牌也可以，权限需手动选择。权限列表见 代码托管平台令牌 （英文）。 一个你已在用并已登录的智能体命令行工具：Claude Code、Codex 或 Gemini CLI。工作进程使用你的订阅运行；Gitoodo 不需要 API 密钥。 处于编排器模式的 Gitoodo； 入门 会带你完成设置。 从议题到合并 议题变为就绪。 来自你信任的人（你自己、拥有写权限的人、所属组织的成员、你的受信任的作者）的议题，在描述完整后，或者一旦带上 ready 标签，就会变为就绪。其他任何人的议题会先收到一个批准问题，绝不会自行启动工作进程。 工作进程启动。 调度器为每个就绪的议题启动一个工作进程，各自在独立的 worktree 和分支中运行，例如 gitoodo/42-login-fix 。它在侧边栏中显示为仓库下面的一个会话，你随时可以接管。 缺少决定时，智能体会提问。 它把问题写进议题；Gitoodo 会在 问我的 中把它显示为一张回答卡片，并预先选中推荐项。你的回答会以一条简短评论发回，工作进程随即继续。参见 问题 。 创建拉取请求。 工作进程推送它的分支，并创建一个带有 Closes #42 的拉取请求。它自己不持有令牌：Gitoodo 用已连接的账户替它推送。议题随之转为 in-review 。 由检查决定。 Gitoodo 从目标分支的分支保护和规则集中读取必需的检查。如果某项检查失败，拉取请求会带着失败信息退回给它的工作进程；如果分支已落后，Gitoodo 会更新它。 合并。 Gitoodo 以你的仓库允许的方式合并（默认为 squash），合并的正是经过检查的那个提交，然后关闭议题并移除 worktree。 一次性设置 必需的检查。 如果没有任何检查，Gitoodo 会等待三分钟看是否出现检查，然后合并。请添加一个 CI 工作流，并在分支保护或规则集中把它设为必需。 安全的自动合并 列出了合并前必须满足的全部条件。 合并账户。 如果你的规则限制了谁可以推送，合并账户必须在该名单上。 允许合并账户 可以添加用户；团队则需要你在 GitHub 上修改。详情见 分支规则 （英文）。 合并方式。 默认值在“设置 → 调度器”中设置，单个仓库自己的方式在该仓库设置的 合并 下设置；参见 合并与发布 。 GitLab：议题与合并请求 在 GitLab 上，工作进程创建的是合并请求。启用 "Pipelines must succeed" 时，由头部流水线决定；在使用快进或半线性合并的项目中，GitLab 会自行变基分支。合并账户需要在受保护的目标分支上拥有 Allowed to merge 。Gitoodo 目前还不读取 GitLab 的分支规则：如果合并被拒绝，会有一张卡片链接到相应设置。 开始使用 下载 Gitoodo ，然后按照 入门 从安装一直走到第一个已合并的拉取请求。

b: Gitoodo 会自行合并工作进程的拉取请求，但前提是你的仓库规则允许。本页列出合并前必须满足的条件、你随时可以叫停的内容，以及究竟谁的文字能够引导工作进程。每一点都链接到详细的参考文档。 合并前必须满足的条件 必需的检查已通过。 Gitoodo 从你的代码托管平台读取它们：GitHub 上的分支保护和规则集，Forgejo 和 Gitea 上目标分支的保护规则，GitLab 上的 "Pipelines must succeed"。如果代码托管平台没有任何要求，拉取请求上报告的每一项检查都必须通过。你还可以在每个仓库设置的合并部分添加自己的检查。 合并的正是经过检查的那个提交。 每次合并都锁定在检查已通过的那个提交上。之后的新推送必须再次通过检查。 必需的评审已给出。 如果你的规则要求批准，拉取请求会等待人来批准，并有一张卡片显示还缺几个。Gitoodo 绝不会批准它自己的工作。 规则允许合并账户进行合并。 否则代码托管平台会拒绝合并，Gitoodo 在规则改变前不再尝试，并在 问我的 中显示一张卡片，说明原因和解决办法，例如 允许合并账户 。参见 分支规则 （英文）。 检查失败时，拉取请求会带着失败信息退回给它的工作进程。真正的合并冲突绝不会被强行处理：拉取请求会收到一条列出相关文件的评论，议题则等你处理。 没有 CI：先把它设置好 如果拉取请求完全没有检查，Gitoodo 会等待三分钟看是否出现检查，然后合并。这样没有 CI 的仓库也能继续工作，但没有任何东西在测试代码。所以，请为每个开启了自动驾驶的仓库配一个 CI 任务，并在分支规则中把它设为必需。设置中的 设置项目 可以添加一个入门用的门禁工作流，你再往里填入真正的检查。 你随时可以叫停的内容 暂缓 单个拉取请求：它会一直等到你放行。 否决 ：它绝不会被自动合并，议题等你处理。两者都在 合并与发布 中说明。 用侧边栏中仓库所在行或其视图中的开关 暂停 一个仓库：那里不会再启动新的工作进程。 标题栏、托盘菜单中的 全部停止 或 Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+H 会一次停下所有内容：没有工作进程运行，不合并任何东西，也不向代码托管平台写入任何内容。 继续 会让每个仓库恢复原样。 有一个限制：已在代码托管平台上开启的自动合并只能在那里停止。 谁的文字会传到工作进程 只有来自受信任的人的议题才会自行变为就绪：你自己、你的工作进程账户、拥有写权限的人、拥有该仓库的组织的成员，以及 受信任的作者 中列出的登录名。其他任何人的议题都要等你批准。 不受信任的人的评论绝不会引导工作进程，也绝不会被当作回答。 不受信任的作者的拉取请求绝不会被自动合并。 带权限检查的工作进程 默认情况下，工作进程运行时不弹出权限提示，因为没有人在场回答，而且只有受信任的文字才会传到它们那里。对于风险更高的仓库，通常是公开仓库，请在该仓库的设置中开启 带权限检查的工作进程 ：这样智能体自己的权限模式和沙盒会作为第二道防线生效。详情见 安全模型 （英文）。 查看发生了什么 状态页 上的活动日志列出了对代码托管平台的每一次写入（包括合并），附有时间、仓库、条目和原因。 开始使用 下载 Gitoodo ，然后按照 入门 操作；你开启自动驾驶时，设置会检查你的分支规则。

t: 并行运行多个编程智能体
h: 一个议题一个-worktree一个工作进程
一个议题、一个 worktree、一个工作进程
通过 SSH 加入更多机器
b: Gitoodo 可同时运行多个编程智能体，上限由你设定，也取决于你的机器能承载多少，每个处理自己的议题，各自在独立的 worktree 中。本页说明工作如何分配、如何设置上限、其他电脑如何通过 SSH 加入，以及 Gitoodo 如何自行清理。 一个议题、一个 worktree、一个工作进程 调度器为每个就绪的议题启动一个工作进程，各自在独立的 git worktree 和分支中运行，例如 gitoodo/42-login-fix 。工作进程之间从不共用工作树。 工作进程启动之前，议题会通过租约被认领，并打上 in-progress 标签。两个工作进程绝不会处理同一个议题，即使在两台机器上也不会。 卡住的工作进程会在同一个 worktree 中重启；在提问或检查失败之后的重启，也会在同一个分支上继续。 正在运行的工作进程在应用及其服务更新或重启后依然存在。 同时运行多少个 总数： 默认两个工作进程，这样首次设置时不会同时在许多仓库中开始工作。你可以在调度器设置中提高上限。 每台机器： 每台机器默认每两个处理器核心运行一个工作进程。在 工作机 下，你可以在 同时运行的工作进程 字段中为性能较弱的电脑设置更小的数字。 在仓库之间公平分配： 每个有就绪工作的仓库都会轮流分到自己的槽位份额。没有仓库能用的槽位会交给就绪工作更多的仓库，因此不会有槽位闲置。带有 priority:p0 的议题优先。 用量限制： 对于 Claude Code 和 Codex，一旦某个用量窗口已用掉 90 %（可调整），就不再启动新的工作进程。达到限制的 Claude Code 会话会等到额度重置后再继续。 所有仓库 的概览显示有多少工作槽位正被占用，以及有多少议题在排队。 通过 SSH 加入更多机器 另一台电脑可以替你运行工作进程。在“设置 → 工作机 ”中用它的 SSH 地址添加它。Gitoodo 通过 SSH 把它的命令行程序复制过去，用 SHA-256 校验和进行核对，并且可以设置好编程智能体。不会开放任何端口，你的代码托管平台令牌也留在你的电脑上：另一台机器使用它自己对代码托管平台的 git 访问权限来克隆和拉取，并把完成的分支发回，由你的电脑推送并创建拉取请求。离线的机器不会分到新工作；它正在处理的议题会在宽限期后释放，交给其他机器。详情见 卫星机器 （英文）。 清理 每次合并之后以及每隔五分钟，Gitoodo 会移除已合并或已关闭议题的 worktree 和本地分支。 在你自己的检出目录中，它只移除它自己的 worktree 和 gitoodo/… 分支。你的分支、stash、索引以及未提交的改动绝不会被动到。 会因此丢失的工作，例如未提交的文件，绝不会被悄悄移除。Gitoodo 会在一小时后把它保存为备份分支，或者把它列在 残留 下由你决定。 没有打开的拉取请求的远程 gitoodo/… 分支会在 24 小时后删除。 关于清理的全部内容见 仓库卫生 （英文）。 开始使用 下载 Gitoodo ，然后按照 入门 操作；第一个工作进程在你自己的电脑上运行，之后可以加入更多机器。

b: 如果你已经在用另一个应用并行运行编程智能体，Gitoodo 最主要的改变是：你不再需要亲自启动每个会话。你的议题就是队列，一旦某个议题就绪，Gitoodo 就会启动一个工作进程。本页展示哪些会变、哪些保持不变，以及如何先用一个仓库试一试。 有哪些变化 用议题取代你手动启动的会话。 你在代码托管平台上或在 Gitoodo 中写议题，或者在对话中描述一个计划，让 Gitoodo 起草议题。每个就绪的议题都有自己的工作进程、worktree 和分支。 问题会主动来找你。 需要做决定的工作进程会在它的议题中提问。你在 问我的 中的一张卡片上回答，而不必盯着终端等提示出现。 拉取请求就是成果。 每个工作进程最后都会产出一个拉取请求，Gitoodo 会在你的仓库要求的检查通过后，以你的仓库允许的方式合并它。 状态保存在代码托管平台上。 标签、评论和拉取请求记录了发生的一切。Gitoodo 根据它们重建自己的视图；即使你不再使用它，工作及其历史也仍保存在代码托管平台上。 哪些保持不变 你的智能体命令行工具及其登录。 工作进程运行你电脑上安装的 Claude Code、Codex 或 Gemini CLI，用你的账户登录，使用你的订阅。Gitoodo 不需要 API 密钥。工作进程的权限和沙盒设置按会话生效，不会写入智能体自己的配置。 你的检出目录。 在你的副本中，Gitoodo 只会拉取，并在它自己的文件夹中添加它自己的 gitoodo/… 分支和 worktree。它绝不会检出、重置或清理你的工作树，也绝不会动你的分支、stash 或其他工具创建的 worktree。 你的代码托管平台和你的规则。 分支保护、必需的检查和评审依然说了算；Gitoodo 会等待它们。 你仍然可以随时介入。 每个工作进程都是一个会话，你可以打开它、接管它、向它发送指令、暂停或取消它。 第一步 下载 Gitoodo ，安装后在引导中选择 编排器 。 连接你的代码托管平台，只开启一个仓库。对于已打开的议题，选择只处理新议题，这样旧议题不会自行启动。 让设置检查你的分支规则并安装后台服务。确保该仓库有一个 CI 任务；参见 安全的自动合并 。 在仓库视图中用 新任务 创建一个小的测试任务，或者给一个现有议题打上 ready 标签。 在仓库下面以会话的形式观察工作进程，在 问我的 中回答它的问题，再看看它创建的拉取请求。 这些都正常运行后，再开启更多仓库并提高工作进程数量；参见 并行运行多个编程智能体 。 开始使用 入门 详细介绍了安装和引导。

。带统计数据的概览不属于其中：它是首页，应用启动时显示它；点击导航的第一项 概览 或左上角的 Gitoodo 标志即可回到它。Gitoodo 会记住你上次使用的子页面，并再次打开它，重启之后也一样。如果你是在某个仓库的视图中关闭窗口的，应用会再次在那里打开。在 所有仓库 编排器通过代码托管平台上的标签来推进每个议题。每组标签只属于一个服务，也只有它会设置。 ready 就绪 可以开始处理。调度器会把它放入队列。 blocked 已阻塞 在等待另一个未关闭的议题。那个议题关闭后，它会重新变为就绪。 needs-clarification 需要澄清 有自相矛盾之处，例如依赖关系或拉取请求的关联。一个智能体会尝试理清。 in-progress 进行中 有智能体正在处理。 in-review 审查中 拉取请求已打开，正在等待检查通过。 needs-human 需要人工 需要你：有问题或审批待处理。 stalled 停滞 尝试三次后仍然失败，正在等你决定。 常规路径：就绪、处理中、审查中、已合并。问题、依赖和故障会分出支路，解决后再回到主路径。 priority:p0 到 p3 决定顺序，p0 最先处理。在 设置 中映射你自己的标签名。 应用中“帮助与反馈 → 帮助中心”里有相同的文字。

所有检查通过后，编排器就会合并拉取请求。在 设置 的 编排 中选择默认合并方式，或在仓库的 仓库设置 中为它单独选择；仓库必须允许该方式。 合并控制 在编排器合并之前暂缓或否决拉取请求。已在代码托管平台上启用的自动合并无法从这里撤回。 在 议题 中拉取请求所在的行用 控制合并 暂停或否决它。快速筛选 已暂停的合并 把所有已暂停和已否决的拉取请求集中在一处，并附带放行按钮。 暂缓 ：拉取请求会等到你放行为止。 否决 ：它永远不会被自动合并，议题会等你处理。 放行 会取消上述任一状态。 已在代码托管平台上开启的自动合并只能在那里停止。 发布规划 发布是每个仓库的一个目标：发布前必须完成哪些议题。在议题列表或发布规划中添加议题（标签 release:next）；依赖项和未关闭的 priority:p0 议题自动属于发布。代码托管平台的里程碑为它命名。 截止日期是一个决策点：Gitoodo 会问你是发布、推迟还是延长。绝不会自动删减任何内容。 仓库是否规划版本，在其详情页中设置。 应用中“帮助与反馈 → 帮助中心”里有相同的文字。

b: 在编排器模式下，专门的服务在后台工作。即使关闭应用，它们也会继续运行。 分类器 读取议题和拉取请求，设置就绪状态和依赖关系，识别你的回答并规划版本发布。 调度器 把就绪的议题分派给工作进程，关注限额和卡住的会话，并合并检查通过的拉取请求。 工作进程 每个议题一个编程智能体，在自己的工作副本中运行。它交付一个拉取请求后结束。 关闭窗口不会停止它们。当你在它们运行时退出 Gitoodo，它会询问该怎么做： 退出 Gitoodo，后台服务继续运行 （议题继续被分派和合并，问题仍会到达）或 全部退出 （应用、调度器和分类器保持关闭，直到你再次启动 Gitoodo；登录系统也不会启动它们）。 不再询问 会记住你的选择；之后可以在“设置 › 通用 › 退出时 ”中改为 询问 、 继续运行 或 一并停止 。菜单栏或通知区域中的 Gitoodo 菜单也提供 停止服务 ，状态总览会显示每个服务的状态。 钥匙串和令牌 你的代码托管平台令牌只保存在系统钥匙串中，从不写入文件。应用及其后台服务读取它们时不会询问，更新后也一样。仅当 macOS 仍然询问时（例如在 App Store 版与直接下载版之间切换后）：选择 允许访问 ，然后选“始终允许”。 在 设置 的 编排 中设置这些服务。如果某个服务没有响应， 服务状态 会显示出来。

b: 最常被问到的问题的简短回答。应用里遇到问题时，请先看 故障排除 。 Gitoodo 支持哪些代码托管平台？ Forgejo、Gitea、GitHub 和 GitLab，也包括自托管的实例，两种模式都支持。你可以同时连接不同平台上的多个账户。 使用智能体需要 API 密钥吗？ 不需要。工作进程和编排器对话运行的是你已经在用的智能体命令行工具（Claude Code、Codex 或 Gemini CLI），使用你自己的订阅。Gitoodo 只检查该命令行工具是否已安装并已登录，从不索要 API 密钥。 编排器和直接模式有什么区别？ 作为 编排器 ，Gitoodo 会把计划拆分成议题，为每个就绪的议题启动一个编程智能体，并合并结果；后台服务负责维护标签和工作队列。每个开启了自动驾驶的仓库都会自行处理它的议题；你可以在它的视图中看到各个会话，需要时再介入。在 直接模式 下只保留 问我的 ：列出等你处理的事项（问题、议题、拉取请求、状态标签），工作由你自己启动。两种模式读取的是同样的议题；可随时在“设置 → 模式”中切换。参见 入门 。 为什么 Mac App Store 版本没有编排器？ 商店的沙盒不允许后台服务和工作进程。编排器随直接下载的版本提供；商店版提供带有 问我的 的直接模式。 我的令牌保存在哪里？ 只保存在系统的密钥存储中：macOS 钥匙串、Windows 凭据管理器或 Secret Service。无界面的服务从 systemd 凭据或服务环境中读取。令牌绝不会写入设置文件、日志、错误信息或应用界面。令牌需要哪些权限以及原因，见 代码托管平台令牌 。 Gitoodo 会连接哪些服务器？ 你配置的代码托管平台服务器、可选聊天通知的 Webhook、仅在你点击发送时才使用的反馈中转，以及匿名使用统计（除非你将其关闭）。包含发送内容的完整列表见 网络清单 。 可以关闭使用统计吗？ 可以。引导的最后一步会显示开关和所发送的内容，之后也可随时在“设置 → 通用”中关闭。完成引导之前不会发送任何内容，统计中也绝不包含仓库名或账户名、内容、令牌或服务器地址。 每个议题都要我自己写吗？ 不用，有两种方式。你可以自己写议题，在代码托管平台上写，或在仓库视图中用 新任务 。也可以让它们自动生成：在 对话 标签页描述你的目标，编排器会起草议题，每个议题是一张带有标题、正文和标签的卡片；只有当你点击 应用 时才会创建议题。Gitoodo 对两者一视同仁：对话使用你已连接的账户来写入，所以无论哪种方式，这个议题都属于你，描述完整后会自动变为就绪，由工作进程接手。参见 对话 。工作进程发现自己议题之外的工作时，也可以提议一个后续议题。Gitoodo 会创建它，并附上指向原议题的链接；它会像你自己的议题一样直接进入队列。如果你想先看每个提议，可在仓库设置的“工作者”下开启 每个后续事项在处理前都需批准 ；之后它会在 问我的 中等你批准。 智能体怎样向我提问？ 需要你做决定的工作进程会在它的议题中写入一个问题块，采用公开的 问题格式 。Gitoodo 会在 问我的 中把它显示为一张回答卡片，并预先选中推荐项；发送后会发表一条简短评论，例如 1b 2 yes 。你随时可以改为在代码托管平台上用普通评论回答。起初列表只显示开启了自动驾驶的仓库中等待的事项，按仓库分组，问题排在任务之前；其余内容收在末尾的提示“另有 N 项来自未开启自动驾驶的仓库 – 显示”之后，并且不计入任何数字。要查看并统计全部内容，请在“设置 → 通知”中开启“也包括未开启自动驾驶的仓库”。参见 问题 。 我需要 gitoodo-questions 技能吗？ 不需要，它是可选的。它教会编程智能体用 Gitoodo 的格式提问。没有它，手写的问题会显示为纯文本，并带有一个自由评论框。对于 Claude Code，请在“设置 → 技能”中安装；对于 Codex 和其他智能体，请把 skill/agents-section.md 中的这一节复制到你仓库的 AGENTS.md 中。 Gitoodo 如何合并拉取请求？ 调度器会在拉取请求完成且检查通过后合并它，合并方式由你在“设置 → 调度器”中选择（默认为 squash），可全局设置，也可按仓库设置。如果仓库不允许该方式，则按 squash、仅快进、合并提交、rebase 的顺序取第一个允许的方式。保留和否决标签可以拦住单个拉取请求；参见 合并与发布 和 调度器参考 。 工作进程可以在其他机器上运行吗？ 可以。其他主机通过 SSH 运行工作进程： gitoodo host add <name> <ssh-target> 会注册一台主机，该主机的 PATH 中需要有 gitoodo 。参见 卫星机器 。 如何更新或卸载 Gitoodo？ 在 macOS 上，再次运行安装命令即可原地更新。卸载命令会删除应用、命令、服务、设置、缓存、日志、已保存的令牌和技能；参见 入门 。 在哪里报告错误或提出功能需求？ 使用“帮助”菜单中的 发送反馈 ，或“设置 → 关于 Gitoodo”中的 反馈 ；只有在你点击发送时才会发出。代码改动请以拉取请求的形式提交到 dev 。

Gitoodo is a desktop app plus a command line with headless services. The forge is the ledger: issues, labels and pull requests hold the whole state, so every picture can be rebuilt from the forge. This page maps the repository; the linked references go into detail. The parts Part Where What it does Core crates/core (crate gitoodo-core ) Forge adapters, settings, sync, secrets, question parsing, orchestration logic. No Tauri, testable on any host. All network access happens here. Command line crates/cli (binary gitoodo ) Classifier and dispatcher services, worker commands ( ask , worker push ), satellites, the MCP server for the orchestrator chat. See the command line reference . App shell src-tauri (crate gitoodo-app ) Tauri 2 shell, kept thin: windows, tray, menus, autostart, commands that call into the core. Frontend src/ React and TypeScript with Vite: the four tabs, settings, onboarding, help center. It never talks to the network and never sees a token. Helper crates crates/pipe-security , crates/scoped-folder Windows named pipes only the current user can open; security-scoped folder bookmarks for the sandboxed Mac App Store build. Website and docs site/ The static landing page and these docs, built with npm run site:build . Data flow Sync. The core polls the configured forges ( crates/core/src/sync ) through one adapter per forge family in crates/core/src/forge : gitea.rs for Forgejo and Gitea, github.rs , gitlab.rs , on shared HTTP plumbing in http.rs (client, auth, error mapping, pagination); the scheduler backs off on errors and throttling. Questions. Comments and issue bodies are parsed for question blocks in the question format . Answers are posted as short comments. Orchestration. The classifier ( gitoodo classifier ) keeps status labels and the work queue for every repository switched on in orchestration.json . The dispatcher ( gitoodo dispatcher ) leases ready issues, starts one worker per issue in its own worktree, and merges finished pull requests. See the orchestrator spec and the dispatcher . App. In orchestrator mode the app reads the picture of the services over a local socket (a named pipe on Windows); in direct mode it polls the forges itself through the core. Secrets Tokens live only in the system secret store (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Secret Service), or for headless services in systemd credentials or the service environment ( crates/core/src/secrets.rs , daemon reference ). They never reach settings files, logs, error messages or the frontend. Workers never hold a token: gitoodo worker push and gitoodo worker pr push and open the pull request through the account connected in Gitoodo. Configuration settings.json (accounts, poll interval, mode, overview labels) is shared by app and command line; orchestration.json switches repositories on and sets states, lease time, label names and the dispatcher block. Both live in the config folder listed in the daemon reference . Where to read on Building : toolchain, checks and the site build. Orchestrator spec , dispatcher , satellites , orchestrator chat . Status model and counters for what the app shows. Network inventory for every connection the app makes.

How to build Gitoodo from source, run its checks and build the website with these docs. Prerequisites Rust (stable, edition 2024). Node.js (current LTS). The Tauri 2 prerequisites for your system: on macOS the Xcode Command Line Tools, on Windows the Microsoft C++ Build Tools and WebView2. App npm ci npm run tauri dev # run the app npm run tauri build # build installers for the current OS The installers land in target/release/bundle/ ( dmg and .app on macOS, msi and nsis on Windows). Builds are made on the target system; there is no cross-compilation. On macOS, bash scripts/build-local-mac.sh [--install] builds the signed app the way a release does. Signing asks Apple's timestamp service for a secure timestamp; when it does not answer, a local build signs without one and says so (the bundler signs ad hoc, the service helper step then signs the bundle with the real identity). scripts/release-mac.sh sets GITOODO_REQUIRE_TIMESTAMP=1 , so a release never ships without one. Every build embeds its identity ( src-tauri/build.rs ): the short and the full commit, -dirty for a modified work tree, the build time in UTC ( SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH when set, for reproducible builds) and the variant direct or store . "About Gitoodo" shows it and copies it for a bug report. Distributors set public build settings such as VITE_PROJECT_URL , VITE_DOCS_URL or VITE_FEEDBACK_RELAY_URL in the build environment or .env.local ( src/core/buildConfig.ts ). They are never secrets; an empty value hides the entry that uses it. Checks scripts/ci-gates.sh runs every repository gate: typos, cargo fmt , clippy -D warnings , cargo test , cargo machete , cargo deny , Prettier, tsc , ESLint (type-aware), Knip, Vitest, the frontend build and the site build with its link check. GATES_FULL=1 makes a missing tool fail instead of being skipped. GATES_FULL=1 bash scripts/ci-gates.sh Single steps: npm run typecheck # both tsconfigs, one after the other npm run lint npm test Website and docs npm run site:build # landing page and docs into site/dist npm run site:links # check the links and anchors of the built docs again site/build.ts builds the landing page and calls site/docs/build.ts , which generates site/dist/docs/ : User pages come from the in-app help ( src/views/help/topics.ts and the texts in src/i18n/ ), the settings structure ( src/views/settings/structure.ts ) and the pages in site/docs/pages/<lang>/ . Every page exists in all six site languages; a language without its own text gets the English one with a note. Developer pages come from the curated documents in docs/ , the pages in site/docs/dev/ and the usage text of gitoodo --help . site/src/docs/registry.ts lists every published document and the reason for every excluded one; a test fails on a new document below docs/ until it is in one of the two lists. Search runs in the browser over one JSON index per language below docs/search/ , served with the pages. There is no external service. Links : the build fails on a relative link to a missing file or a missing anchor. The in-app help links each topic to its page through src/views/help/docsLink.ts ; the address comes from VITE_DOCS_URL (default: the docs of the public website). To preview the result, serve site/dist with any static file server and open /docs/ . Releasing See Releasing for the release steps and how the docs get their version.

b: How a Gitoodo release is built, checked and published (#152, #153, #562, #564). Users download an installer; building from source stays the fallback for people who want it. Assets All files land in target/release/dist/ on the Mac (the Windows files are copied there). The unversioned zip keeps releases/latest/download/... working for install.sh . Linux CLI assets for remote machines ( gitoodo-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu , gitoodo-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu ) need a Linux build host and are not produced yet. Apple silicon only (decision 2026-11-16) Gitoodo for macOS ships for Apple silicon ( aarch64-apple-darwin ) only; there are no Intel ( x86_64-apple-darwin ) or universal builds. Reasons: macOS 27 is the last macOS for Intel Macs and Rosetta 2 ends with macOS 28, so macOS 27 already warns ("App-Update erforderlich") when an app starts Intel code on Apple silicon; and there is no Intel Mac to test on. What this means: release-mac.sh builds and checks ( lipo -archs = arm64 for every binary in the bundle) the arm64 app and CLI only; deny.toml lists no Intel Mac target. install.sh refuses a Mac without Apple silicon; it asks sysctl hw.optional.arm64 , so a Terminal running under Rosetta still counts as Apple silicon. Remote machines ( remote_version.rs , satellite_host.rs ) detect the system the same way ( uname -sm , corrected by sysctl on macOS). b: This document is the single source of truth for the format that agents use to ask a human a question in a forge issue or comment, and for the answer comment that Gitoodo posts back. The parsers ( src/question/ and crates/core/src/question.rs ), the agent skill ( skill/gitoodo-questions/SKILL.md ) and the tests follow it. The examples below are extracted and parsed by a test, so they cannot drift from the parsers. Both question parsers read the examples directly from this document and compare their complete results against tests/question-examples.expected.json . When changing the format, update the examples and their shared expected results together; do not copy example inputs into another fixture. Version 2 replaces version 1; v1 blocks and answers are no longer read. The machine-read parts are fixed and English (markers, kind , Deadline: , Recommendation: , (yes/no) , (multiple) , (text) , the answer tokens yes , no , explain ). The human-read parts (the header line, context, questions, option labels, consequences, reasons) are written in the language Gitoodo writes in on the forge (en, de, es, ar, hi, zh-Hans): the setting "Language on the forge" (the app language, English, the issue's language or a fixed language), which a repository can override. "The issue's language" is read from the issue's title and body without code, links and mentions; when the text is short, mixed or in another language, the app language is used. Readers never depend on that language: answers are understood in every supported language ( yes , ja , sí , نعم , हाँ , 是 , …; see "Answer comment"). The format is an open standard: any agent, tool or forge integration may write and read it without Gitoodo. Its public, versioned home is https://gitoodo.com/spec/questions/v2/ , generated from this document when the site is built. Section anchors are the GitHub-style slugs of the headings ( #answer-comment , #tolerant-reading , #plain-answers ), so links into this document work the same in the repository and on the site. Compatibility promise Version 2 is stable. Within version 2 these never break: A block or answer comment that follows the exact grammar of this document stays valid and keeps its meaning: the markers, v2 , the id and kind attributes, the header, context, Deadline: , question, option and Recommendation: lines, the kind suffixes and the answer tokens ( 1b , 2 yes , 3 "text" , explain ). The machine-read parts stay English and keep their spelling; the block kinds worker , approval and clarification keep their meaning. A reader never demands more than this document demands today, so a writer that follows it is understood by every version 2 reader. The rule for detecting an answered question stays the same, and the forge remains the only source of truth. The one clarification (#764): a comment carrying a Gitoodo machine marker is never the human's reply, even under the human's login (see "Gitoodo comments"). The URL above and its section anchors stay valid for as long as version 2 exists. What may change within version 2: Tolerant reading may accept more slips, words and languages. It never changes how an exact block is read. Explanations, examples and the wording of this document may be clarified without changing a rule. How an app presents a card (layout, hints, controls) is not part of the format. Anything that would break a valid version 2 block or answer gets a new version with its own marker ( v3 ) and its own URL ( /spec/questions/v3/ ). The version 2 page stays published with its rules unchanged. Design goals Works on Forgejo, Gitea, GitHub and GitLab without any server-side support. Reads well as plain Markdown when the app is not used (a human can answer with a normal comment). Machine-readable: the app renders an answer card, the agent parses the answer. Agents write the exact format below; the app reads leniently (see "Tolerant reading") so that slips, hand-written questions and plain human answers still work. Anything that is not clearly a question stays plain text. Nothing ever crashes or half-renders. Question block A block is delimited by two HTML comments. HTML comments are invisible in the rendered Markdown of all four forges, and the text between them renders as normal Markdown (a numbered list with the options as lines below each item). <!-- gitoodo:questions v2 id="<id>" kind="<kind>" --> @<login> **<Name>** (<hint how to answer, e.g. `1b` or `2 yes`>) <up to 3 context lines> Deadline: <YYYY-MM-DD> 1. <Question>? a) <Option> – <consequence> b) <Option> – <consequence> Recommendation: a 2. <Question>? (yes/no) Recommendation: yes <!-- /gitoodo:questions --> Delimiters Opening: <!-- gitoodo:questions v2 id="<id>" kind="<kind>" --> . v2 is the format version; <id> matches [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64} and identifies the block inside its issue. The answer repeats it. <kind> is worker , approval or clarification (see "Block kinds"); both attributes are required, in this order. Closing: <!-- /gitoodo:questions --> . A body may contain several blocks. Ids must be unique per issue; for a repeated id the first block wins. Blocks inside fenced code blocks (``` or ~~~) are ignored, so documentation can quote the format. Block kinds The kind tells the orchestrator (and the app) why the question is asked. It never changes how the block is parsed or answered; the parsed block carries it as kind next to id . Kind Asked by Meaning worker an agent working on the issue The worker is blocked on a human decision and continues after it. approval the classifier A yes/no gate, e.g. for an issue or PR of an untrusted author. clarification the classifier The issue is contradictory or unclear ( needs-clarification ). Unmarked questions (found in running text) have the kind worker . Content All lines are optional, except at least one question. Part Syntax Notes Header @<login> **<Name>** (…) First line. Addresses the human; text after the bold part is free. A login that is no trusted person of the repo (unknown on the forge, no write access) counts as addressed to the user who reads the questions. Context up to 3 plain lines between header and first question More than 3 makes the block invalid. Deadline Deadline: YYYY-MM-DD Among the context lines; does not count as one. At most once. Question <n>. <text> with n = 1, 2, 3, 4 in order 1 to 4 questions per block. Option a) <label> or a) <label> – <consequence> Keys a to d in order. The dash is an en dash or - . Recommendation Recommendation: <value> below the question At most once. Agents should always give one (see the skill). Question kinds The kind is given by an optional suffix at the end of the question line. Kind Suffix Options Recommendation: value Answer token single choice none 2 to 4 ( a to d ) one key, e.g. a 1b or 1bc multiple choice (multiple) 2 to 4 ( a to d ) keys separated by commas: a, c 1ac yes/no (yes/no) none yes or no 2 yes free text (text) none not allowed 3 "any text" A recommendation may be followed by – <reason> ; the reason is ignored. A single choice asks for one option, but the human may combine several: a click in the app picks one option, and an option can be added on purpose (the card's "choose several" control or a Cmd/Ctrl-click). The answer then carries every chosen key like a multiple choice ( 1bc ). Agents read such an answer as "all of these options" (see the skill). The question block itself is unchanged: a single choice still has at most one recommended key. Answer comment The app posts one comment per answered block: <!-- gitoodo:answer v2 id="<id>" --> <answer line> <optional free text, Markdown> Line 1 is the marker with the same id as the block. Line 2 is the answer line: space-separated tokens, one per answered question, in question order: single or multiple choice: number plus the chosen keys in alphabetical order, no separator: 1b , 3ac ; yes/no: number, a space, yes or no : 2 yes ; free text: number, a space, then the text as a double-quoted JSON string ( \" and \n escapes): 4 "Berlin" ; "please explain better", for every kind: number, a space, explain , optionally a space and a note what is unclear as a double-quoted JSON string: 2 explain or 2 explain "What does staging mean here?" (see "Explanation requests"). Questions can be left out (partial answers are valid). Each number occurs at most once. After one blank line follows optional free text, the person's note ("Anmerkung"). It is plain Markdown and not interpreted (see "Notes"). An answer line that does not match this grammar makes the whole comment "not an answer" (it stays an ordinary comment). The tokens are case-insensitive when parsed; the app always writes the lowercase English tokens. Every supported language is understood when reading, in the answer comment and in plain answers: Meaning Words yes yes , ja , sí , si , نعم , हाँ , हां , 是 , 好 no no , nein , لا , नहीं , नही , 否 , 不 explain explain , erklären , explicar , اشرح , समझाएं , 解释 A word ends at whitespace, , , ; , . or a quote; digits and keys ( 1ac ) stay as described above. Explanation requests Instead of choosing, the human can send a single question back with <n> explain when the question, the options or the decision criteria are not understood. It is allowed for every question kind and can be combined with answers to the other questions of the same block ( 1b 2 explain "What does b cost?" 3 yes ). The optional note is a JSON string like a free-text answer; an empty note is written as no note. The agent re-asks exactly the questions marked explain in a new block (new id ) with a fuller explanation of the question, the options and the decision criteria, and keeps the other questions as answered. For the app the block counts as answered like after any other partial answer, so the question is no longer open until the new block arrives, which then shows up as a new question. Notes Every answer a person gives through the app may carry a note: the free text of an answer comment (a question or an approval, also when a whole group of approvals is answered at once) and the note of a finished task (see "Instructions"). Before it is posted the app trims it and normalises line ends to \n ; writes every <!-- as <!-- , so a note can never open a Gitoodo marker (an answer, a question block, the automation marker) or hide text; it renders the same; closes a code fence the note leaves open, so the fence cannot swallow the rest of the comment; caps it at 4000 characters, marking a cut with … . An empty note is left out. Readers take the free text as written; they never interpret it as an answer line. Gitoodo comments The orchestrator may write with the user's own account (no separate worker account), so the login alone cannot tell a worker's question or a status note from the human's reply. Every comment that Gitoodo, its dispatcher, its classifier or a worker posts therefore carries a machine marker on a line of its own: a question block ( <!-- gitoodo:questions v2 … --> ), a lease ( <!-- gitoodo:lease v1 ) or an intake marker ( <!-- gitoodo:intake-rejected --> , <!-- gitoodo:intake-milestone-created --> ), or else the automation marker as the last line: <!-- gitoodo:auto --> . A comment with any of these markers is written by Gitoodo, whatever account posted it. The answer marker ( <!-- gitoodo:answer v2 … ), the forward marker ( <!-- gitoodo:forwarded v2 … ) and the instruction marker ( <!-- gitoodo:instruction v2 --> , see "Instructions") belong to a human acting through the app; a comment with any of them is the human's, even when it also carries a question block (a forward). A comment without any marker is written by a person. h: Quitting the app and the services (#737)
b: gitoodo is the headless side of Gitoodo: the classifier daemon that polls the forges of the configured accounts and a command line that asks it for the queue picture. The app does not need it and works unchanged without it. Commands gitoodo status [--changed] [--json] [--ack] gitoodo service install|uninstall gitoodo classifier gitoodo next --worker session-1 --host win [--repo owner/repo] [--account id] [--json] gitoodo done --worker session-1 --lease <id> [--result "PR ready"] [--json] gitoodo usage [--refresh] [--json] status prints one line per open issue and pull request of the covered repos, grouped like the lage picture: repo, issue#N / pr#N , status labels, age bucket, warnings, title, and a summary line at the end. Issues without status labels show [ohne Einordnung] . --json prints the whole reply ( picture , changed , digest , polled_at , errors ). --changed prints nothing (unless --json ) and exits 0 when the waking lines changed since the last --ack or an issue lacks status labels, 1 otherwise. --ack stores the current state as seen. Typical wake check: gitoodo status --changed && gitoodo status --ack . usage prints the usage of each agent of the dispatcher (5-hour and weekly window, "paused until" at the limit); --refresh first has the dispatcher and every worker machine ask each agent again, as "Check limits now" in the app (at most once per 30 seconds, see docs/orchestrator/dispatcher.md , "Usage limits"). --json prints the providers. Exit code 2: the daemon is not reachable. 64: wrong usage. classifier runs the classifier daemon in the foreground; the service runs exactly this. daemon is a deprecated alias that runs the same thing and prints a note. Classifier role and read model The classifier (spec section 6) polls every repository in state observed (read only), paused and active ; repositories in state off are listed but never read. After each poll it builds a read model in memory and serves it to the app and the CLI over the local socket: request {"cmd":"read_model"} , reply {"reply":"read_model", ...} with polled_at and per repository account_id , full_name , state and the open issues, highest score first. After a start the request waits up to two minutes for the first poll; {"cmd":"read_model", "immediate":true} answers at once instead ( polled_at then is null and repos empty). The app always asks immediate and gives up after 15 s as busy , so a long first poll never keeps its views loading ( read_model_now ); per issue: number , title , html_url , labels , computed readiness ( ready , blocked , needs-clarification , needs-approval , needs-human , in-progress , in-review , stalled , held ), dependencies ( owner/repo#n ), cycle , score and the lease holder if any; readiness uses the dependency graph (open dependencies block, cycles and self-dependencies need clarification, unknown dependencies fail closed), the trust decision of section 5.3 and the label catalog; the score is the dispatcher order of section 7.1 with the weights of the score section of the orchestration config. Request {"cmd":"poll"} (reply {"reply":"poll_scheduled"} ) ends the wait between two polls; the app sends it after the user unlocked or granted a keychain token, so an account that waited for approval is read again at once. Each poll writes its errors to the activity file right before its poll record; rule notes such as "… more questions pending" go to the record's notes , never to labels_set . The types and the client ( ping , read_model , poll_now , request_at ) live in gitoodo_core::service_rpc . The classifier idles at a few MB; an integration test keeps it under 30 MB RSS without accounts. Queue writer and leases The daemon is the only Gitoodo process that writes status labels. next , done and label maintenance share one asynchronous lock, including their fresh forge reads. Run **one writer daemon per repository**; a second host must use that daemon, not start another writer for the same repository. An OS-held daemon.lock in the configuration folder prevents simultaneous writers for the same configuration, even during startup; the OS releases it after a crash. Exactly one classifier runs per configuration (#593, #600): While no service is registered, the app starts gitoodo classifier itself with its process id in GITOODO_PARENT_PID . That classifier (and a dispatcher the app starts) stops within two seconds once the app is gone (quit, crash, update), so the app leaves no orphan. Once the classifier service is registered, the app starts only the service, and a classifier the app started stops by itself and hands over. The service definitions set GITOODO_SERVICE=1 . A classifier service whose lock is still held waits for it instead of exiting, so launchd or systemd do not restart it in a loop; it logs took over the classifier lock when it does. Windows: the parent watch is Unix-only for now; the app's exit stops its children there. Worker identities live inside the local OS-user trust boundary; the dispatcher ([ orchestrator/dispatcher.md ](orchestrator/dispatcher.md)) is the only component that starts workers. Enable repositories explicitly in <config>/orchestration.json (Gitoodo's own configuration): { "repos": [ { "account_id": "nas", "full_name": "owner/repo", "human": "maintainer-login", "releases": true } ], "lease_seconds": 14400, "profile": { "names": {}, "extra_labels": [] } } Missing configuration keeps the daemon read-only. Invalid configuration blocks mutations. Accounts must exist in settings.json ; disabled repositories cannot be assigned. Maintenance runs during polling for enabled repositories, including those outside the dashboard view. next --repo selects an enabled, non-disabled repository. The daemon never edits the config; the only service that does is the dispatcher, which at its start only tidies former start-mode fields and keeps halted as it was. While halted is set, next returns no assignment and the maintenance pass writes nothing ([ orchestrator/dispatcher.md ](orchestrator/dispatcher.md), "Emergency stop"). next and done are the lease commands the dispatcher works the queue with. From the command line ( gitoodo next , gitoodo done ) they never compete with it (#953): in an automation session ( GITOODO_ISSUE is automation:<id> ) both are refused with the code automation_session : an automation reports, it does not take or finish issues; for a repository whose autopilot is on (state active ), next is refused with the code autopilot_on and names the repositories: the autopilot works that queue. done from the command line does not finish a lease in such a repository either (same code). The dispatcher's own requests are not affected; the command line marks its requests with "cli": true . next returns JSON with an assignment (or null when no work is eligible). An assignment contains the full issue and its lease: id, worker, host, account, repository, issue number, expiry and completion flag. Candidates must be open, carry only ready (legacy status:bereit ), have no prd , needs-human (the legacy name an:mensch is not recognised), stalled or extern , and either have no host restriction or a matching host: label. For --host local a host: label matches this machine's name ( orchestration.json › local_host.name , default the sanitised short host name), any of its local_host.aliases and local , without case — the same matcher as the dispatcher ( docs/orchestrator/spec.md , 7.1 item 3). Satellites match only their own configured name. A host: value that names no configured machine but a platform ( mac , win , ubu , ...; see spec 7.1) matches any host running that system. Candidates are taken in the order the app's queue shows (spec 7.1 item 4): the next release and boosted issues first, then by score (priority weight, age per hour, manual boost, release bonus, with the repository's own weights when it has them), highest first; ties go to the earlier creation time, then the lower issue number, then the configured account/repository order. Priorities are priority:p0 .. p3 (legacy prio:1..3 ); an issue without one counts as priority:p2 . Dependencies are declared by a line of their own, in the body or in a comment a person wrote. The line starts (after an optional list bullet - , * , + or 1. and optional bold ** ) with one of Depends on , Blocked by , Waits for , Wartet auf , Abhängig von , Blockiert bis , Abhängigkeit(en) , Depende de or Bloqueado por (any case), an optional colon, and the references, separated by commas, spaces, and or und : Wartet auf: #12, owner/other#3 - **Depends on:** #7 and #8 #12 , repo#12 and owner/repo#12 are supported, including nested GitLab namespaces; the list ends at the first word that is no reference. Anything else is no dependency: a mention in the middle of a sentence, a closing reference, a status line such as Worker fertig: PR #1382, wartet auf gate/nas. and every comment Gitoodo wrote itself (its machine marker, see [ question-format.md ](question-format.md)). A referenced issue or pull request must be verifiably closed or merged; an open, missing or inaccessible one blocks assignment. The app's queue uses the same rule and the same lookup, so such an issue shows as blocked there, never as the queue head. When the dispatcher passes over a ready issue for open dependencies it logs dispatch.skip ( reason dependencies_open , refs the blocking references) once per issue and change, so gitoodo trace owner/repo#n explains the wait. Assignment adds in-progress before removing ready , adds the forge account's authenticated login to the assignees (people already assigned stay; GitHub adds atomically, Gitea/Forgejo and GitLab write the fresh list plus the login), then writes a gitoodo:lease v1 audit comment naming the worker and lease. Worker ids identify sessions, not forge logins. A partial or ambiguous failure leaves the reservation in place. Claims are compare-and-confirm across installs (release-gate review M10): after its lease comment the writer reads the comments again. Every active (not completed, not withdrawn, not expired) lease comment of Gitoodo's own logins posted since the issue was read as ready (plus 10 s for request latency) belongs to the race; the oldest comment wins. The loser posts the same lease again with "withdrawn": true , removes only its own login from the assignees (and only when it added it and the winner is another login), leaves labels alone and backs off for this round. A withdrawn lease never holds an issue. Two installs only see each other's leases when their logins are known writers of the forge host (the same account, or listed orchestrator accounts). done verifies the current audit from the authenticated account (the newest lease comment whose lease was not withdrawn), changes the status to in-review , removes the worker account's assignee and records the result. On an issue that is already closed (the dispatcher closes it with the merge before it reports the run done) it removes in-progress / in-review instead of setting in-review (#848). Repeating an already completed report has no further effects. Leases are reconstructed from forge comments after a restart; they do not depend on the volatile SQLite cache. Rejected reports return JSON reply: "rejected" with a stable code and a human-readable message , exit status 1: foreign_lease , expired_lease , stale_lease , status_changed , invalid_worker , configuration_error , forge_unavailable (server error, rate limit or unreachable forge: worth retrying) or forge_error (any other forge refusal). Expiry is inclusive and never releases the issue automatically. Recovery of expired or partially assigned work is done by the dispatcher's sweeper or by an explicit human decision. A timed-out next may have taken effect; inspect the issue/audit before requesting more work. Label template and hygiene The default profile embeds the English label catalog ( priority:p0 .. p3 , os:* , host:* , needs-clarification , blocked , ready , in-progress , in-review , stal

When a new version needs more
b: Gitoodo needs a personal access token per account. The token wizard (Settings > Accounts > add) and the Replace token … dialog of a stored account name the permissions in the words of the forge's own token page, with the reason for each. This page is the same list for later. The wizard texts live in src/views/settings/permissionGuide.ts ; tests/token-permissions.test.ts fails when this page, the wizard and the checks in crates/core/src/forge drift apart. GitHub Classic token (Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens (classic)); the wizard opens the page with both boxes ticked: Permission Why repo Read repositories and issues, send answers as comments, close issues read:user Recognise which account the token belongs to Fine-grained token: choose the repositories under "Repository access" and set under "Repository permissions": Permission Why Metadata: Read-only List repositories (GitHub grants this automatically) Issues: Read and write Read issues, send answers as comments, close issues GitLab Permission Why api Read issues, send answers as comments, close issues read_api is enough for reading only; without api Gitoodo cannot answer. Forgejo and Gitea Forgejo and Gitea cannot preselect permissions by link. Set them by hand on the opened page (User settings > Applications): pick this access level for each category and leave all others on "No access". Category Access level Why user Read Recognise which account the token belongs to repository Read List the repositories of the account issue Read and write Read issues, send answers as comments, close issues Per mode: orchestrator, working directly, answering The lists above are what answering questions needs. The wizard asks what Gitoodo should do with the repositories, preselects the operating mode chosen in onboarding (or set in the app) and shows one merged list for that mode: each category once, the highest access level wins, plus the role the account needs in the repository. It goes on only after I have set these permissions on the token is ticked; switching to a mode that needs more asks again. The rights per mode come from crates/core/src/forge/rights.rs , the merge from src/views/settings/tokenBlock.ts . Forge Working directly Orchestrator, in addition Forgejo / Gitea repository : Read and write organization : Read and write, only to create or delete repositories in organisations GitHub classic — delete_repo , only to create or delete repositories GitHub fine-grained Contents: Read and write Pull requests, Administration, Commit statuses: Read and write (Administration also creates and deletes) GitLab — — ( api covers creating and deleting) Role in the repository Write (GitLab: Developer) Admin (GitLab: Maintainer), for repository settings such as merge styles and branch protection The organisation scope is optional (#978): Forgejo and Gitea refuse creating and deleting a repository that belongs to an organisation without write:organization , even when the token has write:repository ; GitHub classic tokens delete only with delete_repo . A token without it is still stored and works on every repository; the account in the settings names the gap ("Only to create or delete repos") with Replace token … , and the removal dialog names the scope before the delete is confirmed. A separate orchestrator (worker) account per forge host (#764, docs/orchestrator/spec.md 5.3.1) needs the orchestrator's rights without repository settings ( forge::rights::worker_rights ): no Administration permission and no admin role; write access (GitLab: Developer, Maintainer to merge into protected branches) is enough. Repository settings stay with the user's own account. Creating the worker account automatically ( docs/orchestrator/setup.md , "Automatic worker account") needs more on the own account, only for that moment: Forgejo/Gitea a site administrator whose token has write:admin ; GitLab self-managed an administrator token with api (and Admin Mode where the instance enforces it). Without them the step falls back to the guide; the own token is never asked to gain these scopes for anything else. The worker token it creates has exactly read:user , write:repository , write:issue (Forgejo/Gitea) or api with a 364-day expiry (GitLab). How the check finds out GitHub classic tokens list their scopes in a header and GitLab tokens on /personal_access_tokens/self . Forgejo and Gitea reveal nothing: reading scopes are probed with cheap reads, and the write scopes beyond answering ( write:repository , write:organization ) with a write the forge refuses: an empty body to POST /api/v1/repos/migrate and POST /api/v1/orgs . The forge checks the token's scopes before it reads the body, so a missing scope answers 403 with its name and a present one a validation error; nothing is ever created. Only a named scope counts as missing, so an older forge without scoped tokens reports nothing. GitHub fine-grained tokens reveal no permissions; there the forge names a missing one at the action. The wizard stores a token only when it gives everything the chosen mode needs (writing for working directly and the orchestrator); a token without the optional organisation scope is stored and the gap stays visible on the account. When a new version needs more The check runs when an account is added, its token replaced and synced, and again whenever the accounts in the settings open. If the stored token lacks a permission, the account shows what is missing and offers Replace token … . Replacing a token Replace token … sits on every account in Settings > Accounts (the key icon while the token is fine, a button while it is rejected, missing or short of permissions), on the scope hint and the sync error bar, in the repository rights check, the removal dialog, the status page and the worker account section. It opens a small dialog, not the wizard: one masked paste field (with Show ), a Create token on <host> link (GitHub and GitLab preselect the scopes; Forgejo and Gitea cannot) and the folded permission list. Save sends the token to the core, which: trims it and checks it against the forge; a network or forge error stores nothing; refuses a token of another user (logins compared case-insensitively) and names both logins; reads the scopes: a token without a scope the sync needs is refused, because the account would stop working; a token that only lacks scopes for answering or working is stored after Save anyway (Forgejo tokens cannot be edited later, a partial token beats a revoked one, and the account keeps the gap marked); missing scopes for creating or deleting repositories never stop it; stores it under the same keychain entry. If the write fails halfway, the old token is written back. Nothing is stored before steps 1 to 3 have passed. Afterwards the account's token error and banners clear, its sync restarts, the scope marks and the open rights checks run again. The account keeps its id and every setting; all repositories of the account use the new token, since they share the one keychain entry. The background services (classifier, dispatcher) read the token from the keychain on every cycle, so they use the new token from their next cycle without a restart. On macOS the app then grants the service helper access to the rewritten item where needed (restarting the services only if a grant changed something) and asks the classifier to poll now; on Windows the scheduled task reads the Credential Manager on its next cycle. A token handed to a headless service as GITOODO_TOKEN_<ID> or a systemd credential ( docs/daemon.md ) overrides the keychain and is replaced where it was set. Release rule: a version that adds a required permission lists it in the changelog under "Added" or "Changed" as "New permission required: ...", and the permission appears in the lists above. Closing can also be refused even with write permission: HTTP 412 means forge prerequisites are unmet, for example open issue dependencies. Gitoodo explains this and points to the issue in the browser; it does not remove dependencies or report the issue as closed.

t: States: what Gitoodo shows and what you do about it
h: 2. Issue: where a piece of work stands
3. Worker: one agent on one issue
4. Things Gitoodo repairs on its own
b: Gitoodo is an orchestrator: it takes issues from your forges, hands them to AI coding workers and brings their results back as pull requests. This page is the one map of that flow. Every mark in the sidebar, every session tile, every column in "All repos" and every line on the status page belongs to one of the states below, and each state says whether anything is asked of you (#870). The short version: you act only on "needs you" and "stuck" , and on "in review" when your merge setting leaves the merge to you. Everything else moves by itself: failing checks go back to the worker, and anything left behind is cleaned up by Gitoodo, not by you. 1. Repository: autopilot on or paused Every repository has one switch (#877), in the sidebar and in the settings. State Gitoodo reads Sets labels Starts workers What it means Autopilot on yes yes yes Gitoodo works the repository's issues Paused yes yes¹ no no worker starts; questions still show up ¹ Only in a repository the autopilot worked before; one it never worked stays untouched. "Asked of me" and every counter (header, sidebar, tray, notifications) list what waits for you in repositories with the autopilot on (#897). What waits in paused repositories or in repositories without the autopilot stays behind "N more from repos without autopilot – show" at the end of the list; Settings → Notifications → "Questions from repos without autopilot too" shows it for good. Direct mode always lists every repository. A repository you never want to see is removed from the sidebar ("Remove"); "Show again" in the settings brings it back. Pausing a repository stops its running workers. Their issues go back to ready (the in-progress label is removed), so pausing never leaves work behind. 2. Issue: where a piece of work stands The labels on the forge are the source of truth; the classifier sets them, the dispatcher reads them. A repository row in the sidebar shows at most two marks (#740): the rotating circle in front of its name while a worker runs there, and after its name the "needs you" mark, only while something needs you there (a question or approval, or a stuck issue), with the count when there are several. Everything the autopilot handles by itself gets no mark on the row. The "needs you" mark is a button: with one waiting question it opens that question, otherwise "Asked of me", which lists stuck issues and machine waits with their ways out (#919); the row's menu offers the same as "Open what needs you". A folded group or owner sums its repositories the same way. Hovering the row says, line by line: the repository and its switch; what goes on now, each with its number ("4 workers running · 2 in review"); then each thing that needs you with what to do; then at most one quiet line for the queue ("52 queued", ready and blocked issues together). The screen reader hears the same words. Opening a repository lists up to three lines of current work under it, the running ones first, each with its own mark from the table below. Its filter "Only with open questions or work" keeps the repositories with a question waiting for you, a stuck issue, or a worker running or starting (here or on another machine); blocked, ready, in-review or finished issues and running checks alone do not count (#948). A repository listed twice (under Favourites and in its group) is marked once, in the row it was opened from. Mark Meaning What you do rotating circle Working : a worker is on it right now nothing filled circle with "?" Needs you : a question or an approval answer it on the forge or in Gitoodo; work goes on filled circle with "?" Stuck ( stalled ): the autopilot gave up on it choose a way out on "Asked of me" (see below) filled circle with "?" Stuck on a machine only you can provide choose a way out on "Asked of me" (see below) triangle with "!" Checks fail on the pull request nothing: the worker gets it back to fix them diamond In review : a pull request waits review and merge (or let Gitoodo merge, see settings) circle with a bar Blocked by a dependency or a missing machine nothing: it resolves by itself circle with a dot Claimed by a worker on another machine nothing dashed circle Ready : starts when a worker slot is free nothing check mark Done : a worker just finished nothing Only the two "?" states put a mark on the repository row; the others show in the issue lines under an opened repository, and hovering a line explains it in one sentence. An issue is stuck when its worker made no progress after several restarts, or its checks still fail after the last restart. An issue stalled only because its machine could not start a worker goes back to ready by itself. "Asked of me" lists every stuck issue (#919). A line shows only the reason in a few words and one button, Solve ; it opens the ways out that fit the cause, the recommended one first and marked, each with one quiet line saying what it does: Reason shown Recorded cause Ways out (recommended first) "The worker hung" hung Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "3 runs without a result" no_result Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "Checks keep failing" checks_failing Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "Merging keeps failing" merge_failed Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "Conflicts with the base branch" conflict Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "The branch could not be updated" update_failed Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "The autopilot got no further" no record Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "Working copy was in use" lease_refused Try again (passing), Solve with an agent, … "The base branch moved faster than the checks ran" base_moving Try again (passing), Solve with an agent, … "The agent waited for a sign-in" login_prompt Try again (after signing in), Solve with an agent, … "The agent waited for a confirmation at its start" trust_prompt see below Try again puts the issue back into the queue ( ready , the stalled label goes). It is offered only where another run can go differently, and says why: the cause was passing (a held working copy, a base branch that moved on), it is gone once the agent is signed in again, or an update fixed it. The only cause an update fixed so far is the confirmation at the agent's start (Claude Code and Codex no longer wait for the folder trust prompt since 2026-11-17): a trust_prompt stall from before that offers "Try again" (an update since fixed it) when this app is newer than the fix; otherwise it gets the ways of the other causes. Every other cause repeats, and another run would only spend tokens. The cause decides, not the recorded transient flag (older records call a hang passing). Solve with an agent opens a session of your own ( docs/agent-session.md , "Solve with an agent") in the issue's worktree, with the issue, the cause and the end of the last run as its first message. The issue keeps stalled meanwhile, so the autopilot never takes it. While the session runs, the line says so and offers "Open session". Once it ended, the line offers **Hand back to the autopilot** in one click ( ready ; the next worker goes on from the branch, and the ended session's tile closes); "Solve" keeps the other ways. Pause the autopilot here takes the issue out of the queue: its status goes and extern comes, and the autopilot no longer touches it. To undo it, remove extern on the forge. It replaces "Put back" and is the one way to dismiss an issue without solving it. View issue opens it in its repository. With two or more stuck issues that may be tried again, Try N again above the list tries exactly those (never the ones whose cause repeats), and its hint names why. After a way out the line goes and every count drops at once, before the next poll shows the change. The dispatcher records the cause in stall.json (state folder) when it gives up. Where the end of the worker's screen or transcript shows a prompt the agent cannot pass alone (the folder trust confirmation, a sign-in), that is the cause. Stalls from before the record existed get their cause read once from the dispatcher log of their last run (a refused merge, failing checks, a held working copy, a hang and the prompt it hung at). A worker that sits silent for 20 seconds at such a prompt ends at once instead of waiting out the hang policy and its restarts. A ready issue is stuck on a machine only you can provide (#919) when it waits for: a host: name no machine answers to: "Run on any fitting machine" (recommended, drops host: ), "Use <machine>" for each fitting machine, "Set up <name>" (opens the worker machine assistant with that name); a named machine with another system than its os: : "Set up a <system> machine" (recommended, the assistant asks for that system), "Run on any machine" (with the warning that it may fail), "Pause the autopilot here"; a machine whose coding agent sign-in expired: "Run on another machine meanwhile" (recommended when another machine fits, drops host: ), "Sign in again" (started here when it is this computer and Claude Code, otherwise the command to type there, with a copy button). The question goes away by itself once the sign-in works again. Each says in one sentence why Gitoodo cannot solve it alone. Waits that end by themselves (a machine offline, at capacity, a usage limit) and issues for a system nobody connected yet stay calm: they are no question (#871, #924). 3. Worker: one agent on one issue State Meaning What happens next Running the agent works in its own worktree it opens a pull request or asks a question Silent no output for a while restarted automatically, a few times at most Stalled still silent after the restarts the issue is marked stalled (see above) Ended the agent exited its result is picked up, the worktree tidied Watching a worker: open its repository. The repository view shows every session running there as a live tile, with the queue (ready issues the autopilot starts next) beside them; fewer sessions get larger tiles. A click opens one tile across the full width and resizes the worker's terminal so the agent draws for it; the terminal fills the view and follows new output (scrolled up, "Jump to latest" goes back). A click into it types straight to the agent, every key including Esc, Tab and Ctrl-C; a click outside or Shift-Esc leaves it (#944). "Maximize" (⌘⇧M, Ctrl+Shift+M) lets the terminal fill the window; the same shortcut, or Esc outside the terminal, restores it. Your own sessions (#991) show there too, apart from the workers ( docs/agent-session.md ). "All repos" → "Sessions" shows the sessions of every repository the same way, with one queue across all of them; the "Terminal" button on the "Issues" page opens the same view. 4. Things Gitoodo repairs on its own An orchestrator that runs for weeks meets crashes, restarts and forge hiccups. These states are not yours to clear: Orphaned issue : labelled in-progress but no worker runs it (the dispatcher stopped, a release failed, a machine vanished). The dispatcher checks every minute and puts such an issue back to ready after about five minutes. "Reset" in "All repos" does it at once. Expired lease : a worker's claim that was not renewed is released, and the issue is queued again. Finished worktrees are removed once their work is merged or saved. Unsaved work of a worker that is gone (uncommitted changes, unpushed commits) is pushed as a backup branch after an hour and its worktree removed, on this machine and on further worker machines (#886). What Gitoodo never does alone is discard work. You can save or discard a leftover earlier in "All repos"; nothing else waits for you. 5. Services The status page answers one question: is everything running? This file is the single source of truth for the orchestrator; where it contradicts older docs ( docs/daemon.md , docs/status-model.md , the former integration doc of the external orchestrator, docs/question-format.md ), this file wins and those docs are to be updated. Values marked (default) are configurable. Items marked (proposal) were not decided in detail by the maintainer and may be refined by the implementer; flag deviations in the PR description. 1. Goal and scope Gitoodo grows from a tray app into an open-source orchestrator that runs many Claude Code sessions deterministically across several machines, using a forge (Forgejo or GitHub) as the ledger. Open source, built for other people: all identifiers (labels, services, config keys, markers) are English and configurable. Human-facing text in the app follows the app language; what Gitoodo and its workers write on the forge follows the setting "Language on the forge" (app language, English, the issue's language or a fixed language; a repository can override it, #980). The existing integration of an external agent orchestrator is removed and replaced. It was only the reference for several mechanisms below (worktrees, usage limits, remote hosts). Clean start: no old German keywords or question format. Old German labels are written never and read only as their catalog role ( aliases.tsv , section 5.6). Version 1: classifier, dispatcher with local and remote workers, sweeper, gitoodo ask , answering questions in Gitoodo, orchestrator chat, Claude usage limits in the status bar, release planning (optional per repo). Later: screenshot-based hang detection (screenwatch), mobile app (QR pairing, LAN TLS), GitLab for the orchestrator (the existing GitLab adapter for the plain app stays), releasing dev to main from Gitoodo, AI review of PRs. 2. Principles 2.1 The system never blocks itself Reconstructible: every state can be rebuilt from facts on the forge after a restart, crash or lost cache. Local databases are caches, never the truth. Nothing waits forever: every waiting or locked state has a deadline or a way out and becomes visible to the human at the latest then. Fallback instead of standstill: when a service or path fails, the others keep working (e.g. polling instead of webhooks). Exception: a fallback must never hide a failure. Where it would, use self-start plus a clear error instead of a silent substitute (e.g. the app in orchestrator mode, section 4). Failures stay small: a problem affects one issue or one host, never the whole queue. Every component documents where it can block and how it heals (blockade tables below). The main host is not always on. When it is off, the system stands still; this is intended. After waking, every service first reconciles with the forge, then acts. 2.2 Facts and labels The forge is the only source of truth. Services write facts (comments, assignees, PRs, lease audit comments, question blocks) and labels. Each label group has exactly one owner – the component that makes that decision. Nobody else writes labels of that group. Owners recompute their group from the facts on every run and overwrite it; there is no "conflict resolution". Services are deterministic. LLMs run only inside workers and the chat. 3. Architecture 3.1 Components Name Binary / command Job Not responsible for Gitoodo (app) Gitoodo.app (binary renamed internally to gitoodo-app ) GUI, orchestrator chat, questions, status hosting services, writing service labels Classifier gitoodo classifier readiness, dependencies, PR links, answer detection, release planning starting workers, merging Dispatcher gitoodo dispatcher assigning issues, starting/stopping sessions, limits, hang detection, PR auto-merge classification labels, writing code Sweeper gitoodo sweeper removing merged branches and worktrees deleting unmerged work Ask gitoodo ask a worker's question to the human waiting for the answer Satellite gitoodo satellite hosts worker PTYs and the sweeper on a remote host scheduling MCP server gitoodo mcp the chat's tools file or shell access Attach gitoodo attach <issue> view/interact with a running session in any terminal – Worker a Claude Code session (no own binary) one issue, one worktree, PR labels, other workers, merging to main Forge adapter library in gitoodo-core uniform API for Forgejo and GitHub business logic Ledger Forgejo or GitHub (exactly one forge per project, configured per repo) issues, labels, PRs, milestones, branch protection running services One program gitoodo with subcommands; each service runs as its own process and system service, started and stopped independently. Today's gitoodo-cli becomes gitoodo . Shipping (#355): the direct-distribution app bundles the CLI as a Tauri sidecar ( bundle.externalBin , overlay src-tauri/tauri.sidecar.conf.json , built by scripts/build-sidecar.sh ). Installing copies it to a stable per-user folder ( paths::bin_dir , GITOODO_BIN_DIR overrides) and registers classifier and dispatcher there as system services with automatic restart (launchd KeepAlive , systemd Restart=always ; Windows: classifier only, task with restart on failure; the dispatcher needs named-pipe control first). The app shows app, installed CLI and running classifier versions and offers a reinstall on a mismatch. The sandboxed store builds ( store feature) ship no sidecar and install no services: they are a viewer and the orchestrator runs from the direct build or a manual CLI install. Today's daemon ( docs/daemon.md ) is split: queue/lease logic moves into the dispatcher, label hygiene into the classifier. Destructive catalog transfer on activation is dropped (section 5.6). Where things run: main host – classifier, dispatcher, sweeper, local workers, app. Satellites – gitoodo satellite (workers + sweeper), controlled by the main host's dispatcher over SSH. Forge adapters in v1: Forgejo and GitHub. Capabilities: issues, labels, comments, dependencies, branches, PRs, auto-merge, milestones, events/webhooks with polling fallback (default 5 min). 3.2 Communication App ↔ services: local socket / named pipe (as today's daemon: mode 0600, user-only pipe). Dispatcher ↔ satellite: SSH only (stdio bridge, JSON lines). No open ports on satellites. Workers never talk back to the dispatcher directly; they write to the forge ( gitoodo ask , PRs). Writes from the app (answers, approvals, chat actions) go straight to the forge; in orchestrator mode the app then nudges the classifier to re-read immediately. 4. The app Two modes , selectable in the app, with the consequences explained in the UI: Direct mode: the app polls the forges itself, as today. No orchestrator, no label maintenance; status is derived from assignees and PRs. Orchestrator mode: the app shows the services' picture via the local socket (classifier: issues/labels; dispatcher: workers, queue, leases, hosts), plus chat, worker control and limits. If the services are down, the app tries to start them; if that fails it shows a clear error state instead of data. It never silently falls back to direct mode. Repositories: connect a forge, Gitoodo lists all repos, the user switches them individually or in bulk. In the app a fetched repo is on (fully autonomous) or off ; pausing is an action on a repo that is on, not a level picked during setup (#599). Stored states: off (not fetched, disabled_repos ), observed (shown as "off": fetched, nobody writes; default for newly imported repos), paused (on and paused: classifier works, dispatcher assigns nothing), active (on). The stored values need no migration: observed reads as off, paused as on + paused, active as on. Switchable in the app and by chat (project focus, e.g. "only A and B now"). Questions: questions on which other issues wait are sorted first and show the number of waiting issues. After 2 h (default) unanswered – or the question's own deadline – Gitoodo notifies again. Status bar: per Claude login the remaining 5-hour and weekly limit with reset time; when locked, clearly when work resumes; stale values are marked as stale. Viewing sessions: live terminal view of any worker (local or remote) in the app. 5. Ledger: labels, questions, trust 5.1 Label catalog Names are canonical defaults; users can map them to their own names. The app guides you through the orchestrator setup and does each step for you. On first start the onboarding offers orchestrator mode (preselected) next to the plain to-do list. With orchestrator mode, the onboarding sets up every repository picked in its repo step in one go, right after that step: you choose once what happens to issues that are already open and press Set up now . Gitoodo then installs the background service (the signed release reads tokens through the service helper without any keychain step; other builds grant the services access once, macOS may ask: choose Always Allow ), renames legacy labels and creates missing ones, switches each repo on, clones missing local copies into the clone folder, installs the skill for the worker agent and starts the dispatcher. Each part and each repository shows its own state; Try again repeats only what failed. Own label names, single repositories and agent instructions stay in the settings. First run (#337) The onboarding leads a first-time user from the account to a running worker: Repos to work on : every repository Gitoodo reads starts switched off. The step lists them unchecked, with search and "All"/"None"; only the checked ones are set up and switched on. A repository switched off here (or later in the settings) does not show in the sidebar. Setup : one confirmation sets up all checked repositories. Each shows its label preview (kept, renamed old → new , created) before anything is written, then its progress; Try again repeats only what failed. Legacy labels are read under their catalog meaning; nothing is deleted. The open-issue choice defaults to Check existing issues and ask : open contributions of other authors are never trusted on their own, the intake asks for an approval, which "Asked of me" answers per group or all at once. The merge style is preselected from what the repositories allow (Forgejo repositories that only allow fast-forward get fast-forward-only ). Workers : this machine is listed as a worker with its capacity (default 2, editable) and the agent found on it; machines named in host: labels that do not exist are listed with the issues waiting for them and can be made an alias of this machine. How it goes on : the live state (dispatcher, workers, ready issues), then either **Release an issue** (sets the ready label on an open issue of a switched-on repository) or **Create a test task** (a small issue that is ready at once), and where progress shows (board, sidebar, status). Switching a repository on records adopted_at . Every switched-on repository can be paused and switched on again where it shows: the play/pause button on its sidebar row (on hover and in the "…" menu) and in the board's repository header. Both write the same state as Settings → Repositories ( active / paused in orchestration.json ); pausing lets running workers finish. A short message confirms each switch. The emergency stop keeps its state across restarts: what ran when the app ended runs again, what was halted stays halted (a banner says so, with "Fortsetzen", which lets every repo continue in its own state). "Alles anhalten" in the title bar, in the tray menu, Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+H or gitoodo stop-all stops everything at once (see dispatcher.md , "Emergency stop"). Switching on more than three repositories at once asks first and names the count and how many workers run in parallel ( dispatch.max_workers , default 2). The sidebar picks several repositories at once: Shift-click picks a range, Cmd-click (macOS) or Ctrl-click (Windows, Linux) adds or drops one, Shift+arrow extends from the keyboard, Cmd/Ctrl+A picks every shown repository and Escape lets go. A bar at the foot of the list and the "…" menu then pause, switch on, star or move all picked repositories ("Pause 3 repos").
