Every counter in Gitoodo shows a value of one Counts value, computed in Rust ( crates/core/src/sync/counts.rs , SyncHub::counts in src-tauri/src/sync.rs ). The webview never counts on its own; it reads get_counts once and follows the counts event. Counter Value Tray title and tooltip total Tab "Fragen", header total + refused merges + status Heading "Fragen" questions , tasks , approvals Bundle "Freigabe" open approvals (#705) total = questions + tasks + approvals , so the single tab shows the tray number. Approvals of foreign contributions ( intake-approval-* cards) are no questions: the heading counts them apart, and the bundle above the list holds them. Tasks for the human are waiting items without a valid open question block ( needs-human with a description and maybe a - [ ] acceptance list, e.g. a step in a developer portal only a person can do; crates/core/src/human_task.rs ). They ask for a hands-on step, not a decision: the list shows them in their repo's group after its questions with the tag "Aufgabe" (#897), the sheet as "Aufgabe" with the checklist, "Erledigt" and "Zurück an den Orchestrator" (both with an optional note "Anmerkung (optional)"; on a hand-back the note is the person's instruction to the worker, see "Instructions" in docs/question-format.md ), and the heading names every kind that waits ("6 Fragen · 3 Aufgaben · 161 Freigaben"; only questions: "6 Fragen warten auf dich"). There is no inbox of forge notifications any more (#189): Gitoodo never fetches or marks forge notifications, and only waiting items are counted. The header shows no count (#84): each number appears once, on its tab. One "needs you" (#919). The header's overall state ("3 need you"), the badge on "Fragen an mich" and what that page lists on landing are one set, and a click on the header's number always lands on that page while the number is above zero: total (questions, tasks and approvals in scope, see "Autopilot scope" below), issues the autopilot gave up on ("Hängt fest", label stalled ) in repos with the autopilot on, listed on the page with their reason and "Try again", "Put back" and "View issue" (#919, see docs/states.md ). They are no approvals any more: a worker ran on them, so the issue never reads "waits for your approval" ( intake::reason ), ready issues in repos with the autopilot on that wait for a machine only the user can provide (an unknown host: , a machine with the wrong system, an expired agent sign-in), one each, listed on the page with their ways out ( repoNeeds(…).hosts , #919). The status part "workers" no longer counts these ( statusWaitCount ), so nothing counts twice, merges a repository setting refuses and the user still has to fix ( waitingBlocks , #942), the parts of the status only the user can fix ( countedParts : a rejected sign-in, a keychain approval, ready issues waiting for a worker machine, a service that does not answer, …), each shown as a card with its fixing action at the top of the page. A disk running low is left out (#970): it has its own entry in the status bar, its own notification and its problem on the status page. The repo part (questions in scope that are not answered yet, plus stalled issues and machine waits only the user can resolve in scope, repoNeedsCount ) comes from one place, repoNeeds over the sidebar's activity ( src/views/sidebar/repoActivity.ts ): the repos' marks ("3 issues need you") add up to it, and the header, the badge and the page use it, so the header always equals the sum of the repos' marks plus refused merges plus status problems, which have no repo mark. needsYouTotal in src/views/shell/overall.ts adds them up; landing in src/views/questions/landing.ts is what the page lists, and needsYouCount.test.ts pins both to each other for a mix of questions, tasks, approvals, refused merges, machine notices, stalled issues, machine waits and repos with and without the autopilot. A way out taken on the page takes its issue out of every count at once ( markResolved in useRepoWorkspace.ts , for at most five minutes until the read model shows the change). Repos without the autopilot never feed the number : their questions, tasks and approvals wait behind the page's quiet "N more from repos without autopilot – show" at the end, and that N is never added anywhere. The tray title shows only total : refused merges and status problems have their own notifications there. Tray and webview are updated from the same Counts in the same call ( publish_counts ), after every poll, after answering or commenting, and after removing an account. Rule Questions : open entries of all "waiting for me" views that count in the tray, over all accounts, minus questions answered through the app (answer card or free comment) whose waiting_since is not newer than the posted comment. Such an answer is dropped at the next poll once the question has left the list or waits again. The popover shows the same questions teal ("handled"). Kind ( account_counts , mirrored by waitKind in src/views/questions/tasks.ts ): an entry whose newest card is an intake approval is an approval; one without an open question block is a task; every other entry is a question. Each entry counts once. Overview (#237, #933), the start page: statistics only. It lists no questions and shows no "needs you" number; that number lives in the header and on "Fragen an mich". Repo rows with an open question (same rule) carry a mark without a number. No sidebar filter changes that number. Disabled repos (#135): items of repos switched off in the settings are in no list, no counter, no unseen mark and no system notification. They are dropped centrally ( without_disabled , read by SyncHub::tally and the snapshot events), so switching a repo off updates tray and lists at once; switching it on shows its items again (after the next sync for what the poll skipped). Ungated repos (#705): approvals of repos this app's orchestrator lists as observed or paused are in no counter and no list ( without_ungated , from Config::ungated ), since nothing works on them there; the paused intake asks no new ones. Repos it does not list keep their approvals. The other questions of those repos count as before. Autopilot scope (#897): in the orchestrator mode only repos with the autopilot on ( active in orchestration.json , Config::autopilot ) count. What waits in paused, observed or unlisted repos is in no counter, no unseen mark, no reminder, no chat notice and no system notification ( within_autopilot in SyncHub::tally and SyncHub::counted , within_scope for the toasts); the sidebar sets no "needs you" mark there either. The snapshot event names the repos ( autopilot ), so "Fragen an mich" lists those first, grouped by repo with the questions before the tasks, and keeps the rest behind "N weitere aus Repos ohne Autopilot – anzeigen" at the end. The direct mode and the setting asked_all_repos ("Fragen auch aus Repos ohne Autopilot", Settings → Notifications) count every repo ( autopilot is null ). Switching a repo's autopilot or the setting republishes counts and snapshots at once; an unreadable orchestration file hides nothing. List filters (search, repo, kind, status; #61) never change any counter. They narrow what a list shows, not what waits; otherwise the tray (which knows no filters) and the popover would disagree. Under an active filter only the head of the view says "shown of total" (e.g. "3 of 12 questions need you", #109); without a filter it shows the total. A failing account keeps its last good entries, so its counts stay stable until the next successful poll. Paging: every list request follows the forge's Link header ( collect_pages ), so counts are not capped at one page of 50. Seen and unseen Every counted item (open question) is either seen or unseen ( crates/core/src/store/viewed.rs , unseen_keys in counts.rs ). Seen means the item was visible in the opened list: its row stayed at least 60 % in view for about 0.7 s while the window was focused and visible. The webview only reports the keys ( mark_seen ); Rust looks up the item's activity time and stores it as the mark. New activity makes it unseen again : a question whose waiting_since is newer than its mark is unseen. Answered (handled) questions are never unseen. Snooze ( snooze_question , unsnooze_question ): a snoozed question leaves the list, the counters and the unseen marks until its wake-up time (presets: 1 hour, tomorrow 09:00 local, 1 week; computed in src/state/snooze.ts ). It returns by itself at that time (timer plus every poll), without restart. New activity on the issue does not wake it early. Stored per account in viewed.json ( snoozed , unix seconds); expired or vanished entries are pruned on the next poll. Tray : one unseen item turns the tray check red (macOS and Windows); the tooltip names how many, e.g. "Gitoodo (3, 1 unseen)". Counts.unseen carries the number. Lists : unseen rows carry a small neutral ink dot (6 px) and a hidden "Neu"/"New" for screen readers, never red. A dot stays while the user looks at the list and is gone once the window loses focus, so it never vanishes under the user's eyes. Persistence : marks live in viewed.json next to the settings and survive restarts. Marks of items that left the lists are dropped at the next poll; a removed account is forgotten. Local only : viewed.json is not part of the settings export and is never sent anywhere. System notifications A system notification appears only for a new hit of a "waiting for me" view that counts in the tray (assignment and labels as set in the criteria editor, #143). A plain new issue that no counting view matches never notifies, neither does a hit in a view that does not count, and an item in two counting views notifies exactly once (the hits are de-duplicated by repo and number in fetch_account ). The first poll after a start is the baseline and notifies nothing. Covered by the tests in crates/core/src/sync/fetch.rs . Where a click leads (#939) Every notification carries its target, and a click brings the app forward and opens it there: Notification Opens New question (poll, dispatcher, reminder) the question's card over "Asked of me" Several new questions (summary) "Asked of me" Worker stalled, merge failed, merge vetoed the issue or pull request on its repository's page Issue waits for its worker machine Settings → Worker machines Invalid orchestrator settings the status page Low disk space (#970) Settings → Storage Usage limit warning nothing beyond the app (no single place to open) The target holds only kind, account id, owner/name and number, never a token. The core keeps the last clicked target until the window takes it ( take_notification_target ) and announces it with the event notification-open , so a window that opens only because of the click still finds it. Per platform: macOS: the target travels in the request identifier of the UNNotificationRequest ; a delegate of UNUserNotificationCenter reports the click ( crates/scoped-folder/src/notification.rs ), also when the click started the app. Windows MSIX (store build or installed package): the toast's launch arguments carry the target; its Activated handler reports a click while the app runs. A click after the app ended starts it without the target (no toast activator is registered). Direct Windows install and Linux: the notification plugin reports no click, so a click only brings the app forward, as the system does by itself. Every alert of the dispatcher is worded in the app language (title and body); a question names its first line, else the issue title, never the dispatcher's log text. On a question alert the app reads that one issue again at once ( fetch_issue , the same filters as the full poll) and posts the notification only once the list has the question, or after 5 s at the latest; the poll that later finds the same question does not announce it a second time. Gitoodo writes a structured log to help explain what happened on a user's machine (for example a token check that failed, a worker that did not start, or a sync that keeps failing). The app and every background service (classifier, dispatcher with its worker supervision, satellite) use the same module ( crates/core/src/logging ) and schema. The log never contains tokens, Authorization headers, response bodies, or URL paths and queries; servers are logged as host[:port] only. Location One folder per user, shared by the app and the services: System Folder macOS ~/Library/Logs/de.gitoodo.app/ Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\de.gitoodo.app\logs\ Linux $XDG_STATE_HOME/gitoodo/logs/ ( ~/.local/state/... ) GITOODO_LOG_DIR overrides the folder; with GITOODO_STATE_DIR set (tests, isolated runs) it is <state>/logs . The test-access build keeps its own folder under its identifier. File Writer gitoodo.log the app classifier.jsonl gitoodo classifier (also when the app starts it) dispatcher.jsonl gitoodo dispatcher , including the workers it supervises satellite.jsonl gitoodo satellite (not the --stdio bridge) <service>.stderr.log stderr of a service (bootstrap errors, a crash before logging started) runs/<run_id>/… terminal transcript of one worker run (see Worker transcripts ) Each process owns its file through a sidecar lock ( <file>.lock ). A second process of the same kind (for example a classifier service waiting for the app's classifier) writes <name>-<pid>.<ext> instead, so two processes never rotate one file. Each line is one JSON object (schema v 2): { "v": 2, "ts": "2026-11-16T11:00:11.175Z", "seq": 12, "level": "warn", "proc": "dispatcher", "pid": 4711, "component": "dispatch", "event": "dispatch.host_wait", "cid": null, "run_id": null, "issue": "owner/repo#42", "span": null, "audit": false, "msg": "waiting for a host; no matching host can take it", "ctx": { "host": "mac-mini", "reason": "offline" } } ts : UTC, RFC 3339 with milliseconds. seq : line number within the process, so gaps show dropped lines. proc : app , classifier , dispatcher or satellite ; pid the process ID. event : stable name; service events are dotted ( <area>.<what> ), app events keep their earlier names. msg is human text, never parsed. cid is a correlation ID: every line of one sync run (or one command) shares it. A cid field on an event (a classifier decision the dispatcher refers to) is lifted out of ctx . run_id , issue and span are top-level for every line ( null when unknown): a field of that name on an event is lifted out of ctx . run_id and span are reserved for timed worker runs (see Runs and steps ). ctx holds the remaining typed fields (at most 32), each redacted. Levels Level Meaning error Unrecoverable failure the user relies on (token check failed, keychain write failed) warn Failed, but retried or carried on (sync failed, integration error, keychain read failed) info State changes (sync finished, settings changed, audit events) debug Detail (sync started, every keychain access) Dependencies log only warn and error . Rotation, budget and retention Per file: 5 MiB, then the file becomes <file>.1 (older generations shift, beyond .3 they are deleted): at most 4 files and 20 MiB per process. A line that would not fit after a failed rotation is dropped rather than written past the cap (on Windows a file held open by a viewer cannot be renamed; Gitoodo then copies and empties it, and if that fails too it drops lines and retries after 30 s). The next written line reports the count as dropped_line . Whole folder: a disk budget, default 75 MiB (setting log_budget_mb , 20–500), covering every log and stderr file in the folder and one level of subfolders. Files older than 14 days (setting log_max_age_days , 1–90) are deleted. When the folder is over budget, the oldest files that no running process writes are deleted first. *.stderr.log files are emptied above 1 MiB. When: at the start of every process and every 6 h after ( log.cleanup names what was removed). Files of a running process are never deleted; their size is bounded by the per-file cap. gitoodo diagnose shows the folder's size against the budget. Lines with the same host, method, endpoint and kind are throttled like other errors (see Throttling ). A request that succeeds after failed attempts logs forge.request_recovered ( attempts ). A 404 is an answer the callers handle (a deleted issue, an optional route), so it is logged at debug and counted in forge_not_found , not in forge_failures . The forge_* fields count, since the last summary: forge_requests sent, forge_cached reads answered without a request, forge_not_modified conditional reads the forge answered with 304, forge_failures failed attempts (rate limits included), forge_not_found 404 answers, and the retry wait and latency percentiles. A classifier poll reads each forge route once per account: inside the poll, repeated GETs (the reconcile pass, the queue snapshot and the read model read the same listings) are answered from memory, and a write to a repo makes the poll read that repo again. Replies with an ETag (GitHub, GitLab) are kept across polls and asked with If-None-Match . Forgejo and Gitea send no ETag ; there the comments of an issue whose updated_at and comment count did not change are reused for up to 10 minutes. The cache lives in process memory only, keyed by a fingerprint of the credential, never by the token itself. Logs name the API family neutrally: gitea-compatible covers Forgejo and Gitea, which share the API and are not told apart without a signed-in request. Runs and steps One attempt of the dispatcher at an issue is a run with its own ID, r- and 10 lowercase Crockford base32 characters ( r-7k2m9q4xzt ). Every line of the attempt carries it in run_id , whichever process writes it: The classifier logs classifier.ready with a fresh cid when an issue becomes ready and keeps that decision ( cid , since when) in the read model while the issue stays ready. Issues that are ready when first seen get their decision too, but their lines are debug and one classifier.ready_seen line counts them. The dispatcher creates the run ID when it picks the issue up and logs run.start with that cid , host , worker and agent , so the run is linked to the decision. The ID is stored in the worktree lease, sent to a satellite in the spawn request and given to the worker as GITOODO_RUN_ID . Satellite lines of the worker (its worktree, spawn and satellite.worker_exit ) carry it, and so does the main host's delivery ( pr.open ) of a satellite branch. The pull request itself does not carry it. run.end closes the run with duration_ms and result : merged , stalled , needs_human , parked , paused , user_stop , start_failed , lease_refused , host_gone or skipped . Each step is a span. A step that runs within one call is logged as span.start and span.end ; a step that already happened ( queue.wait , host.select , merge ) as one span.end . span.end always has duration_ms and result ( ok , error , cancelled , timeout ); otherwise also error_kind and, where useful, error (redacted). A run that ends with steps still open ends them with the run's outcome. Gitoodo shows every text in one language, chosen in Settings → General → Language. The window, the tray menu and tooltip, system notifications, user-facing errors and chat webhook messages always follow the same language and switch together at runtime, without a restart. Supported languages Tag Language Own name Direction Intl locale de German Deutsch left to right de-DE en English English left to right en-GB zh-Hans Chinese (Simplified) 中文（简体） left to right zh-Hans-CN hi Hindi हिन्दी left to right hi-IN es Spanish Español left to right es-ES ar Arabic العربية right to left ar German is the reference shape of the catalogue; English is the fallback. Choosing the language The setting is System or one of the tags above. It is stored in settings.json ( language ) and therefore part of the settings export and import (see settings-backup.md ). The frontend mirrors it in localStorage because the texts are needed before settings.json arrives. System walks navigator.languages and takes the first supported language. Regional variants map to their language: es-MX → es , zh-CN , zh-SG and zh-Hans → zh-Hans , ar-EG → ar , de-AT → de , hi-IN → hi . Traditional Chinese ( zh-Hant , zh-TW , zh-HK , zh-MO ) and every other language fall back to English. The picker shows each language in its own name, regardless of the current language. How texts are organised src/i18n/<namespace>.ts holds German and English for one area of the app ( shell , questions , dashboard , detail , settings , filter , permissions , native , support ). src/i18n/catalogue.ts lists the namespaces. src/i18n/locales/<tag>.ts holds one further language for all namespaces. Its type is Translation , so a missing or extra key is a compile error. t("namespace.key", vars) returns a text; {name} marks a variable. Numbers passed as variables are formatted in the digits of the language. tp("namespace.key", count, vars) returns a plural text. A plural is an object with one entry per CLDR plural category the language uses ( zero , one , two , few , many , other ); Intl.PluralRules picks the entry. Arabic uses all six, Chinese only other . Dates, times, relative ages and numbers go through Intl ( formatDate , formatDateTime , formatAge , formatNumber ). Never build them by hand. Texts shown by Rust The native namespace holds the texts of the tray menu and tooltip, system notifications and chat webhook messages. The frontend resolves them in the current language and sends them with the language's digits to the set_ui_texts command at start and on every language change ( src/App.tsx ). Rust rebuilds the tray menu right away and fills the placeholders itself. Until the first push, English applies. User-facing errors reach the frontend as categories and are translated there. Right to left Arabic sets dir="rtl" and lang on the root element. To keep the layout correct in both directions: Use logical CSS properties ( margin-inline-start , padding-inline-end , inset-inline-start , text-align: start , border-inline-start ), never left / right . Horizontal motion multiplies by var(--dir-sign) ( 1 or -1 ). Icons that point along the reading direction ( back , chevron ) are listed in DIRECTIONAL in src/ui/Icon.tsx and mirrored by src/ui/Icon.css . Repository names, issue numbers, code and URLs stay left to right inside the text; wrap them in <bdi> or set dir="ltr" where they stand alone. Question format keywords The keywords of the question format ( Recommendation: , Deadline: , (yes/no) and the others in question-format.md ) are part of the machine-readable format and stay English in every language. Only their explanations in the UI are translated; answers are read in every supported language. Language on the forge What Gitoodo writes on the forge has its own setting (#980), Settings → Language → "Language on the forge" ( forge_language in settings.json ): app (default), issue or one of the six tags. A repository can override it in its repository settings → Questions ( forge_language of the repo in orchestration.json ). It covers the intake and approval questions and notes ( crates/core/src/orchestration/intake_texts.rs ), the answer hint of question headers, the fixed lines the app posts (finishing a task, the AI summary label, the suggested forward note; src/views/detail/forgeLang.ts ) and the worker brief, which names the language for question blocks, status notes and pull request texts. Code, commit messages and repository files follow the repository's own rules. app follows the app language. The services have no window, so System uses the language the window last resolved ( window_language in settings.json , written by the window, never by a settings save); before the first window, English. issue detects the language of the issue's title and body ( crates/core/src/forge_language.rs ). Code, links, mentions, issue references and identifiers are left out first. Arabic, Devanagari and Han script must make up at least 70 % of the letters (with a minimum length); Latin text needs at least eight words and enough common words of English, German or Spanish, clearly ahead of the other two. A short, mixed or other-language text falls back to the app language. The machine-read parts of the question format stay English in every case. Adding a language Add the tag to LANGS in src/i18n/define.ts (the order is the order of the picker). Add its Intl locale to LOCALES and its own name to ENDONYMS in src/i18n/index.ts . If the language is written right to left, extend direction . Map regional variants in matchLang if the base tag alone is not enough (as for Chinese). Create src/i18n/locales/<tag>.ts with export const <name>: Translation , translating every key. Give each plural the categories the language needs. Keep every {placeholder} and keep question-format keywords German. Register it in tables in src/i18n/index.ts and in the language union in src/core/types.ts . Add the variant to Language in crates/core/src/store/settings.rs (with a serde rename if the tag is not plain lowercase) and extend its test. Add the tag to SAME_AS_ENGLISH in src/i18n/i18n.test.ts with the keys that are intentionally identical to English (brand names, hosts). Run npm test : the guard checks key parity, plural categories, placeholders and untranslated values. Then check the layout in the real app at 400 px width for clipped labels. Translation style Natural and concise, as a native speaker would write a UI; no word-by-word translation. Labels must fit the 400 px window. Product name "Gitoodo" and forge names (GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo) are never translated.

Gitoodo can write its settings to a JSON file, read them back on another machine or after a reinstall, and undo the last import from an automatic backup. The UI lives in Settings → Backup ( src/views/settings/BackupPage.tsx ); the logic is in crates/core/src/store/transfer.rs and the Tauri commands in src-tauri/src/transfer.rs . File format { "app": "gitoodo", "schema_version": 2, "settings": { "...": "..." } } Field Meaning app Always gitoodo ; any other value is rejected as a foreign file. schema_version Settings schema the file was written with. settings The stored settings, accounts included, without any secret value. Older files are migrated in memory on import; the preview says so. Files from a newer schema are refused instead of being guessed at. The export is written atomically, so an interrupted export never leaves a half file behind. Suggested file name: gitoodo-settings-YYYY-MM-DD.json (local date). Secrets Tokens and the chat webhook URL live only in the keychain and never appear in an export, a backup, a preview or a log line. After an import, accounts whose token is missing in this machine's keychain show a "Replace token …" action ( accounts_needing_token ). The usage statistics choice and its random install ID live in usage.json , not in the settings, so they are never exported, imported or backed up: an imported settings file leaves the statistics undecided on the new machine, and a restored backup never brings back an install ID that was deleted by switching the statistics off ( docs/privacy.md , "Usage statistics"). Import in two phases Preview ( preview_settings_import ): the file is read, validated and migrated without changing anything. The preview lists the names of changed settings (never their values), added and removed accounts, accounts without a token and whether a migration ran. Apply ( import_settings ): after the user confirms, the current settings are written to the backup first, under the settings lock. If the backup fails, nothing is replaced. Then the imported settings are saved and theme, global shortcut and sync loops restart with them. Validation beyond the field types: every account needs a non-empty, unique id, a login and an http(s) address with a host. Automatic backup and restore Every import writes the previous settings to settings.backup.json next to the settings file. settings_backup_time returns the backup's time (Unix ms) or nothing; the UI shows it or a "no backup" hint. restore_settings_backup backs up the current settings before restoring, so a restore can itself be undone. Limits and errors Reason When too_large File over 1 MiB; it is refused without reading. not_json Not valid JSON. foreign_file app is not gitoodo . newer_version Schema newer than this build supports. invalid_content Validation failed; detail capped at 200 chars. no_backup Restore without a backup. io File access or encoding failed. The frontend maps these to its own rejection keys ( rejection() in src/views/settings/transfer.ts ) and shows a calm, localised message. Import, export and restore are recorded as audit events without content. Test IDs settings-backup-export , -import , -preview , -preview-migrated , -confirm , -confirm-yes , -cancel , -status , -renew , -restore , -restore-none , -restore-time , -restore-open (all prefixed settings-backup ).

One rule for every file and folder the app reads or writes (settings, state files, backup, logs, export and import files): Follow links for reading and writing, absolute or relative, for single files and for whole folders (config/data folder, log folder). Never replace a link with a file. Atomic saves write the temp file next to the link's target and rename it over the target; the link stays. Corrupt-file recovery leaves the link in place and copies the target's content to <name>.corrupt next to the link. Never delete a link target. Log rotation of a linked gitoodo.log copies the content to .1 and empties the target; deleting rotated files removes only the link itself. Refuse where following is unsafe. A dangling link or a link loop is reported as an error ("points to ... which does not exist; nothing was written" / "loops back on itself"); nothing is created at the link's target. Logging swallows the error and retries later. Implementation: crates/core/src/links.rs ( resolve_link ), used by store/fsutil.rs and logging/writer.rs . Export and import go through the same helpers, so the path returned by the file picker may be or contain a link. Platforms Linux/macOS direct build: covered by unit tests (linked file, linked folder, relative, dangling, loop). macOS sandboxed store build: a link outside the container only works if the user granted access to its target; the scoped-folder bookmark must be created for the resolved folder. Not verified on a device (documented only). Windows: symlinks and junctions are followed by the OS for folders; file links are resolved by resolve_link . Creating them needs developer mode or admin rights, so the tests are Unix-only. Not verified on a device (documented only).

How the popover window is framed per platform and build type, and why the App Store build stays free of private API. Code: src-tauri/src/frame.rs and frame_macos.rs (native side), src/ui/tokens.css (block "Window frame"). Per platform Build Frame Corners macOS direct transparent window over Liquid Glass (macOS 26+) or the popover material rounded, 12 pt macOS App Store solid, the page paints --color-bg , normal window shadow rounded, 12 pt Windows 11 solid rounded by DWM Windows 10, Linux solid square Plain browser solid (no data-frame from the shell) n/a The shell sets data-frame="vibrancy" or data-frame="solid" on <html> through an initialization script, so the first paint already matches. Only vibrancy lets the material show through; every other value keeps the solid tokens. Store build: no private API A transparent webview needs WebKit's private key drawsBackground (wry sets it whenever Tauri asks for transparent ). App Store review rejects private API, so the store build keeps an opaque webview and only rounds the window ( Frame::Rounded ): The main window is declared with "create": false in tauri.conf.json and built in frame::create_main . Transparency and effects are only requested when frame_for(Platform::Mac, store = false) returns Vibrancy . The store build (Cargo feature store ) never calls transparent , so the private key is never touched and the frame is the normal opaque window. macOSPrivateApi stays off in every config. Corners: frame_macos::round_corners gives the window's content view a layer ( NSView.wantsLayer ) with CALayer.cornerRadius = frame::CORNER_RADIUS , cornerCurve continuous and masksToBounds , so the webview is clipped. The window turns non-opaque with a clear background ( NSWindow.isOpaque , NSWindow.backgroundColor = NSColor.clearColor ): only the clipped corners are see-through, the page still paints --color-bg behind every pixel, so the frame stays solid (also with Reduce transparency). Shadow: kept on ( NSWindow.hasShadow , then invalidateShadow ). For a non-opaque window macOS derives the shadow from the drawn pixels, so it follows the rounded corners; the square outline of the direct build does not occur here because there is no effect view in the square frame. No unsafe : the NSWindow is looked up among NSApplication.windows by comparing it with Tauri's ns_window() handle, so no raw pointer is dereferenced. All calls are safe objc2 bindings ( objc2-app-kit , objc2-quartz-core ); kCALayerCornerCurveContinuous is passed by its documented string value continuous instead of reading the extern static. No window-vibrancy setCornerRadius and no NSVisualEffectView / NSGlassEffectView in this build; translucency there is a separate spike. The string drawsBackground still exists in the binary as a constant in wry's code; that branch only runs for transparent , which the store build never requests. It is no Objective-C selector ( __objc_methname does not contain it). Public API used (Apple documentation): NSView.wantsLayer , NSView.layer , CALayer.cornerRadius , CALayer.cornerCurve , CALayer.masksToBounds , NSWindow.isOpaque , NSWindow.backgroundColor , NSColor.clearColor , NSWindow.hasShadow , NSWindow.invalidateShadow() , NSApplication.windows . macOS direct build Effects list [LiquidGlassRegular, Popover] , state Active , radius frame::CORNER_RADIUS (12 pt, mirrored as --radius-window ). Tauri applies the first effect the system supports: macOS 26 and later: NSGlassEffectView with its public cornerRadius . macOS 15 and older: NSVisualEffectView with the popover material; the corner radius goes through window-vibrancy's undocumented setCornerRadius . Acceptable only because this build is not reviewed by Apple; it is the second reason the store build stays solid. No window shadow ( shadow(false) ). macOS computes the shadow from the square window frame, not from the rounded material, which left a square dark outline around the corners. The page paints a veil over the material ( --color-window , 55 % of the solid ground) so text keeps the solid contrast values in light and dark. Dark mode adds a 1 px light inner edge so the window separates from dark wallpapers without a shadow. The veil sits on #root with border-radius: var(--radius-window) , never on body : with a transparent <html> , a body background propagates to the whole square canvas and fills the corners. Reduce transparency ( prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce ): macOS draws the material opaque and the veil switches to --color-bg , so the window is solid with the regular contrast. Windows and Linux Opaque windows with the page background. Windows 11 rounds undecorated windows itself (DWM, shadow: true from the config). Windows 10 and Linux stay square; no effect API is used there. Since the frame is solid , the page never draws an inner card here: the popover is the DWM-rounded window itself, and the detached window is a normal decorated window with the page edge to edge (checked on Windows 11, light and dark, #248). Resizing The popover keeps its tray-anchored, title-bar-free look and can still be resized by dragging any edge or corner. Code: src-tauri/src/window_size.rs , tray::place_main , core store/window.rs . Native resizing, no extra grip: the window is "resizable": true with "decorations": false . macOS: tao uses the style mask Borderless | Resizable , so AppKit offers the invisible resize edges and corners of a normal window, in both builds. Windows: tao hit-tests the undecorated window ( WM_NCHITTEST ) and, with the DWM shadow on, keeps the invisible resize borders outside the page, so every edge and corner works. Bounds: at least 400 x 320 logical points ( minWidth / minHeight in tauri.conf.json ); at most the work area of the screen the tray icon is on ( set_max_size each time the window opens). store::fit_size applies both bounds to the remembered size; on a screen smaller than the minimum the minimum wins and the placement keeps the top-left corner on screen. Size: the popover always opens in the remembered size (default 400 x 680 until the user resizes it); the page never reports a content height and nothing resizes the window on its own. Placement: tray::place_main gives the window its fitted size first and then centres it below (menu bar) or above (bottom taskbar) the tray icon with that size, clamped to the work area, so it never leaves the screen. Without an icon rect the positioner plugin places it as before. Persistence: window.json in the app config directory (logical points, versioned like the other stores, corrupt or missing file gives the default). The size is stored when the window hides and when the app quits, only if the user changed it: a size the app shrank to fit a smaller screen does not overwrite the wish for a larger one. Local to the installation: settings export and import do not carry it. Reset: Settings, General, "Window size", button settings-window-size-reset (command reset_window_size ) stores the default and resizes an open window in place at the tray icon. Frame at any size: the vibrancy material (direct build) and the content view's rounded layer (store build) resize with their views; the store build recomputes its pixel-derived shadow after every resize ( frame::resized , NSWindow.invalidateShadow() ). The page has no fixed widths; lists, detail and settings fill the extra space, centred empty states keep a readable measure. Detached window The popover can become a normal app window, for a longer look at the overview. Code: src-tauri/src/window_mode.rs , core store/detached.rs . Detach: header button shell-detach or Cmd+Shift+D (macOS) / Ctrl+Shift+D (Windows, Linux), command detach_window . The same window changes its style, so the page keeps its state: title bar, task bar entry (Dock icon on macOS), not always on top, freely resizable (at least 400 x 320, no upper bound) and no longer hidden on blur. The tray icon and its click keep working and bring the window to the front. Back: header button shell-attach , the same shortcut, or closing the window (red button, Alt+F4). The window hides and turns back into the popover; the app keeps running in the tray. Quit stays in the tray menu. Frame: position and size are stored in detached-window.json whenever the window goes back (and before quit), in logical points of the desktop. store::place_detached reopens it there when enough of it lies on a current screen (shrunk to that screen), otherwise at 900 x 700 centred on the main screen (shrunk to its work area on a smaller screen). Local to the installation like window.json . End of the onboarding (#617): its fixed, centred window (never stored as the frame) becomes the detached window in the stored frame, else the default, and stays in front ( finish_onboarding_window ); the overview and the pending introduction tour open in it, or the setup assistant after an orchestrator run. Closing it returns to the tray like any detached window. It does not switch back to the tray panel: on macOS that made the app an accessory app, which resigned it active, and the blur dismissed the freshly shown panel at once, so nothing appeared. Size: a size the user dragged is the stored frame; the popover keeps its own size in window.json , so switching back restores the popover size and switching again restores the window frame. Frame per build: the detached window always has the system title bar, shadow and corners, and its content runs edge to edge below the title bar, without the popover's inner card. Switching the mode switches the native frame too ( frame::apply_mode ): the direct macOS build swaps the rounded Liquid Glass / popover material for the square window background material (follows the active state), the store build drops its 12 pt content clip, Windows and Linux keep their solid native frame. The page drops its drawn corners and edge via data-window="detached" (tokens.css). Title bar on macOS (#617): framed windows (detached, onboarding, the test build) get a transparent title bar without its title, the page reaching up beneath it ( frame::title_bar , frame_macos::overlay_title_bar ). An empty unified toolbar makes the bar 52 pt tall, so the window buttons sit centred beside the page's top bar: the header with the lockup, or the onboarding's brand bar with the lockup and phases. The page learns it through data-titlebar="overlay" and keeps --titlebar-inset (physical left in every language) free for the buttons and --titlebar-height as its minimum height. The inset is where the zoom button ends plus 14 pt (#741): frame_macos::window_buttons_end measures it natively and hands it over as --titlebar-buttons-end when the bar switches on and after every resize (so 0 in full screen, where the buttons leave the bar); without a measurement the page assumes 80 pt (macOS 26/27). Both bars are data-tauri-drag-region="deep" : dragging moves the window, a double click zooms it, buttons keep their clicks (capability core:window:allow-start-dragging , core:window:allow-internal-toggle-maximize ). The popover switches it all off again. Windows and Linux keep the system title bar. The page learns the mode from get_window_mode and the window-mode event ( popover or detached ); in detached mode it reports its height but the window keeps the size the user chose. Test build The test build (Cargo feature test-access , "Gitoodo Test") starts with its window open and never hides it on blur, so automation can drive it without a tray click. h: Prompt timing and behaviour when denied
Notifications on macOS: prompt shown in the background (#166)
Background services read the token without a prompt (#369)
b: Which permissions Gitoodo needs on macOS and Windows, per build type, when the system asks, what the app does when the user declines, and where the decision comes from. Principle (Apple HIG "Privacy", Microsoft "Windows app privacy guidance"): ask in context, only when the feature needs it, explain calmly before the system prompt, and never block the app when a permission is denied; show a hint that leads to the system settings. Build types: macOS direct: Developer ID, hardened runtime, notarized, not sandboxed ( Entitlements.direct.plist ). macOS App Store: sandboxed ( Entitlements.appstore.plist , Cargo feature store , config overlay tauri.appstore.conf.json ). Windows direct: unpackaged installer, full trust. Windows MSIX: packaged for the Microsoft Store ( src-tauri/windows/AppxManifest.template.xml ). Matrix Purpose macOS direct macOS App Store Windows direct Windows MSIX Network to forges (HTTPS) no entitlement needed com.apple.security.network.client none capability internetClient Forge on the local network Local Network prompt ( NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription ); ATS NSAllowsLocalNetworking same, plus network.client none (firewall prompt is the system) privateNetworkClientServer Skill install into agent skills folders writes directly (not sandboxed) folder dialog ( files.user-selected.read-write ), explanation first writes directly writes directly ( runFullTrust ) Desktop control (Agent Desktop) Accessibility and Screen Recording for Agent Desktop, once per Mac; see Agent Desktop not available (no npm, no SSH in the sandbox) a signed-in, unlocked session not available in the Store build Notifications UNUserNotificationCenter , authorization at start or first send; denial shown same (sandbox needs no entitlement) no prompt; hint to Notifications settings same Start at sign-in LaunchAgent via the autostart plugin; hint to Login Items SMAppService.mainApp (macOS 13+) autostart plugin (registry) windows.startupTask , see store Menu bar / tray only, no Dock icon LSUIElement LSUIElement none none Tokens Data protection keychain (group entitlement + profile), file-based fallback; see Keychain same group; see Keychain Credential Manager, no prompt Credential Manager, no prompt Prompt timing and behaviour when denied Local network (macOS): the system asks on the first connection to a local host. The app does not pre-prompt. When the connection to a local forge fails, the wizard shows a calm note with the action "Systemeinstellungen öffnen" ( Privacy_LocalNetwork ). Only shown for local hosts on macOS ( local_network_hint_applies ). Notifications (macOS): Gitoodo asks for alert and sound authorization at start once an account and a notification type are set up, and again before every send (the system only prompts while undecided). The settings page reads the state the same way: on a denial it says so ("Mitteilungen sind ausgeschaltet"), otherwise it keeps the general note; both lead to the Notifications pane. See Notifications on macOS . Notifications (Windows, Linux): the Tauri notification plugin reports the permission as granted, so a denial cannot be detected; the page keeps the general note with the action "Systemeinstellungen öffnen" ( ms-settings:notifications ). A failed send is logged. Start at sign-in: toggled by the user on the autostart page. When it fails (denied or pending approval in Login Items), the page shows the error with the action "Systemeinstellungen öffnen" ( com.apple.LoginItems-Settings.extension , ms-settings:startupapps ). First-run onboarding (#94, #617): shown on first launch, whenever no account exists, and from "Hilfe & Feedback → Erste Schritte". It runs in its own centred window (980 x 680, clamped to the screen; its frame is never stored as the window frame) with named phases on top: Willkommen, Konto, Repos, Arbeitsweise, Mitteilungen & Start, Fertig. Enter runs the main action and Esc goes back, except in text fields. The repo step switches repos on or off with the same disabled_repos as Settings → Repos and leaves orchestration rules alone. Its notification step asks only on the button "Mitteilungen erlauben" and shows the denied hint with the Notifications pane; its autostart step (on by default) shows the same error and Login Items action as the autostart page. Progress is stored in the settings ( onboarding ), so every step can be skipped and an interrupted run resumes; closing the window pauses it and the next tray click reopens it. Finishing ("Zum Überblick", or "Orchestrator einrichten" for the setup assistant) turns the window into the regular detached window ( finish_onboarding_window , see docs/window-frame.md ), where the overview and the introduction tour (or the setup assistant) follow. Skill folder (App Store build only): the skill page explains why ~/.claude is needed and what is written (only gitoodo-questions ), then opens the folder dialog. A folder not named .claude is rejected with a hint; cancelling changes nothing. The direct build skips this step. The system settings deep links are in src-tauri/src/permissions.rs ( settings_url ). Notifications on macOS (#131) Symptom: on macOS 27 no notification appeared and Gitoodo was missing from System Settings > Notifications. Root cause: the Tauri notification plugin (2.x) posts through notify-rust and mac-notification-sys , which use the deprecated NSUserNotificationCenter . Before the first post, mac-notification-sys looks up a bundle id with an AppleScript ( get id of application ... , blocked in the sandbox and failing anyway), falls back to com.apple.Finder / com.apple.Terminal and swaps the implementation of NSBundle.bundleIdentifier . Notifications were therefore posted under another app's identity; Gitoodo never registered with Notification Center and never asked for authorization. The plugin spawns the post and returns success, and its desktop permission check always answers "granted", so nothing was logged. Fix: on macOS the plugin is not linked any more. src-tauri/src/notify_macos.rs uses UNUserNotificationCenter through the safe objc2-user-notifications bindings (no unsafe ): requestAuthorizationWithOptions (alert, sound), then addNotificationRequest with a unique identifier. It only runs inside an .app bundle (an unbundled cargo /dev binary would make the center raise); outside, a warning is logged and nothing is posted. Failures are logged as notification_error with a reason ( authorization_failed , rejected , no_app_bundle ), never with the notification text. Windows and Linux keep the plugin and now log a failed send. Limits: the error object of a failed request is not read (that would need unsafe ), so the log has the reason but not the system's error code. The permission state comes from the authorization answer, because reading UNNotificationSettings from its completion handler also needs unsafe . There is no notification-center delegate, so a banner may be held back while Gitoodo's own window is in front. Notifications on macOS: prompt shown in the background (#166) Symptom: after #131 the permission request did not appear and Gitoodo was missing from System Settings > Notifications. Evidence (unified log of the installed, Developer ID signed, sandboxed /Applications/Gitoodo.app , macOS 27.2): usernoted registers the bundle at the first request ("Sending request for permission for <bundle id>"), but the prompt record is alertStyle:"none" with response action: closed and the settings read authorizationStatus: Denied ; the authorization was only set to "allow" seven seconds later, by hand. Signing, bundle identity and sandbox are therefore fine: the center is reached ( Creating a user notification center , didGrant ) and later banners were delivered ( Presenting ... alertStyle:"banner" ). The app log has no notification_* event because nothing failed. Cause: the request is made at start from a menu-bar app ( LSUIElement , accessory policy) that is not the active app, so the system shows the prompt as a quiet banner that closes by itself. It is counted as not allowed, and the user never saw a dialog. Fix: the first authorization request of an installation (marker file notification-prompted in the config dir, notify::first_prompt ) activates the app first ( NSApplication.activate , main thread, safe bindings), so the prompt is shown to the user. Later requests stay silent. Not reproducible here without wiping the notification database, so the fresh-install check (prompt visible, entry in System Settings > Notifications, question and #73 reminder as banners) needs a human on a clean install. Open: without a notification-center delegate a banner is still held back while Gitoodo's own window is in front (needs unsafe , which the crate forbids). Keychain Tokens and the chat webhook URL live in the OS credential store ( crates/core/src/secrets.rs ). On macOS the app uses the data protection keychain (#126): items belong to a keychain access group and carry no per-app access list, so the direct, App Store and dev builds that share the group read the same token without any prompt (TN3137, "Sharing access to keychain items"). The group is Q7V3X27S2U.de.gitoodo.app (team id plus bundle id), the first keychain-access-groups entry, hence the default group of new items; the code sets no group. The direct build lists the group of the former identifier online.lindstedt.gitoodo (Gitoodo 0.1.x, #595) second, only so the one-time move ( crates/core/src/identity_migration.rs ) can copy the tokens out of it without a prompt; its Developer ID profile allows Q7V3X27S2U.* . Remove that entry once no 0.1.x install is left ( scripts/check-identifier.py allows exactly this line). Items of older versions live in the file-based keychain and are described below. Entitlements. keychain-access-groups is restricted: the data protection keychain needs keychain-access-groups or com.apple.application-identifier , and both must be authorized by an embedded provisioning profile (TN3125, TN3137). A signed app that claims them without a matching profile is killed at launch, so they are not in the default plists. The extra plists ( Entitlements.direct.keychain.plist , Entitlements.appstore.keychain.plist ) and the overlays src-tauri/tauri.keychain.direct.conf.json / tauri.keychain.appstore.conf.json (add --config after the usual config) set the entitlements and embed the profile from src-tauri/profiles/{direct,appstore}.provisionprofile (ignored by git, account specific). The sandbox of the store build needs no further keychain entitlement. Without the profile (plain build, dev, ad hoc) the app gets errSecMissingEntitlement (-34018) and uses only the file-based keychain; the prompt hint stays. Builds with the entitlement keep a shared copy there for exactly these builds (see "Migration and mixed builds"). Profiles (Apple Developer account). Created 2026-11-10 through the App Store Connect API (global key in ~/.config/appstoreconnect/api_key.json , POST /v1/bundleIds and POST /v1/profiles , types MAC_APP_DIRECT with the Developer ID Application certificate and MAC_APP_STORE with the Apple Distribution certificate); the portal steps below are the manual equivalent. The App ID did not exist yet and was created with the same call. The App Store profile expires 2027-04-19 with its certificate and must be recreated then. Since #595 (2026-11-16) the App IDs are de.gitoodo.app and de.gitoodo.app.service with Developer ID profiles for both; an App Store profile for de.gitoodo.app does not exist yet: Identifiers: App ID de.gitoodo.app exists; no extra capability is needed for keychain sharing on macOS (the group is derived from the team id and the profile's application identifier). Profiles, "Developer ID" (macOS): create a Developer ID provisioning profile for the App ID with the Developer ID Application certificate; save as src-tauri/profiles/direct.provisionprofile . Profiles, "Mac App Store Connect": create a profile for the same App ID with the Apple Distribution certificate; save as src-tauri/profile

t: Test access: driving the app without a human
h: A real test repository beside the fixture
Check that every element has a test ID
Restore the desktop after a test
b: The normal app is a tray panel: no window until a tray click, dismissed on blur, hidden from the accessibility tree. The test access build removes those obstacles so a worker can operate it with Agent Desktop ( agent-desktop , see below). It is a separate Cargo feature ( test-access ); release and store builds contain none of it. What the test build changes: Window mode : a regular, decorated window, visible at start, never dismissed on blur. The app is a Dock app, so agent-desktop list-windows lists it as Gitoodo Test . It opens in the detached window's frame (remembered, else 900 x 700 centred, clamped to the screen; #363), not in the popover size ( docs/window-frame.md , "Test build"). Own identity : bundle ID de.gitoodo.app.testaccess , own config and log directory. It runs next to the installed app and never touches it (single instance, keychain, settings). Test account : a fixture forge ( fixture/demo , user tester ) and an in-memory token store. No real token, no network, no keychain. The account keeps the fixed id acc-fixture across restarts, so per-account state such as folded groups persists; other accounts are removed. Test IDs in the accessibility tree : each data-testid is mirrored into the DOM id (Agent Desktop's native_id of kind ax_dom_identifier , searchable with find --native-id ) and into aria-roledescription . An element that already has its own id (label association) keeps it. Notifications : the permission reads as granted; posts are logged as test_notification . Usage statistics : hard stop. The test build, like any run with GITOODO_UI_AUTOMATION=1 , records, writes and sends nothing, whatever the onboarding switch says ( docs/privacy.md ). Build and start VITE_TEST_ACCESS=1 npx tauri build --debug --bundles app \ --features test-access --config src-tauri/tauri.test-access.conf.json open -n "target/debug/bundle/macos/Gitoodo Test.app" The panel is open right away. Nothing needs a tray click. Address elements by test ID Scripts use Agent Desktop. Point GITOODO_AGENT_DESKTOP at it (default: agent-desktop on PATH, which Gitoodo installs as ~/.local/bin/agent-desktop ); the scripts in this repo never hardcode its location. Workers go through gitoodo desktop [--on NAME] <command> instead, which waits for their turn at that machine's desktop and reaches another machine's desktop over SSH ( dispatcher ). agent-desktop find --app "Gitoodo Test" --native-id shell-settings --first # exact test ID agent-desktop click @<snapshot>:e<n> # ref from the line above Every command prints one JSON envelope; matches carry ref_id ( @<snapshot>:e<n> ), role , name and native_id . Refs belong to one snapshot; the test ID does not change. snapshot --app "Gitoodo Test" prints the whole tree ( --max-depth 50 for deep screens). Ref actions are headless: they neither move the pointer nor take the focus. Look again after each action. One session at a time uses a desktop. Workers take turns through gitoodo desktop-turn ; a script is run while nobody else uses this desktop. Fixture content: three questions in fixture/demo . #1 has a question block with a deadline (tomorrow), #2 is free text, #3 has a deadline two days in the past (the overdue label of the list, #73). GITOODO_TEST_EXTRA_QUESTIONS=<n> at start adds n free-form questions (#4 on, at most 200) to check many open questions (#237). Rows are questions-row-… , copy and share buttons are questions-copy-… and questions-share-… , the detail screen uses detail-… . For long-string layout checks (#337), set GITOODO_TEST_LONG_TEXT=1 . Every fixture title (default and scale mode) gains a long sentence and one long word without break opportunities, so wrapping, clipping and ellipses show at the minimum window size. Bodies, numbers and labels stay unchanged. For large-list navigation (#337), set both GITOODO_TEST_REPOS=300 and GITOODO_TEST_ISSUES_PER_REPO=5 in the test app's launch environment. This replaces the default fixture with 300 repositories ( fixture/scale-001 through fixture/scale-300 ) and 1,500 distinct issues. Each issue is assigned to tester , has needs-human and a cycling ready , in-progress , in-review or blocked status label. Question bodies reuse the three default question types. Each repo also has two fixture pulls, with the green pull linked to that repo's first issue. Dashboard groups and counts come through the normal Rust adapter and sync path. Both values must be positive integers; missing, invalid or zero input keeps the default fixture and its existing extra-question behavior. Valid scale inputs are capped at 300 repos and 20 issues per repo (6,000 issues total); GITOODO_TEST_EXTRA_QUESTIONS is ignored in scale mode. The scale dataset is seeded once at startup. Repo names, forge IDs and issue URLs are unique; issue numbers are globally unique within this fixture. Comments and closures are scoped to their repository and remain in memory until exit. Other unsupported adapter mutations stay unsupported. This creates test data, not a performance result; navigation and responsiveness still need an explicit runtime check. Showcase data for screenshots GITOODO_TEST_FIXTURE_LANG=de or =en replaces the fixture with an invented open-source team in that language ( src-tauri/src/test_showcase.rs ): two repositories ( kiezwerk/pegelstand and kiezwerk/radkeller , in English harborlight/tidewatch and harborlight/trailkit ), four questions to the user (one with a deadline tomorrow, one free text, one overdue, one approval), the board with three running workers, pull requests (one with a failing ci/test ), a week of closed issues and merged pulls for the weekly review, eight weeks of throughput, the readiness checklist of a well kept repo and a scripted orchestrator chat that proposes one comment. Workers, usage, setup checks and the chat are answered by the fixture, never by a running classifier, dispatcher or agent. A simulated dispatcher ( src-tauri/src/test_showcase_dispatcher.rs , #915) gives each session a live terminal over the real attach protocol (backlog, a step line every few seconds, typed keys echo back) and applies steering: Hold and Resume mark the worker held, an instruction appears in its terminal, Cancel, Stop and Park end it, Restart counts a restart. Any other value keeps the plain fixture above. GITOODO_TEST_SHOWCASE_SESSIONS=N (with the showcase) runs N sessions in total instead of three, at most 24: the extra ones are in-progress issues numbered from 300 in both repositories, for checks of a crowded session grid. GITOODO_TEST_WEEKLY_REVIEW=1 (with the showcase) makes the weekly review due at start. The status bar shows the version only in every build; commit and build time are on the About page. The landing page's shots in site/shots/ come from the browser demo ( scripts/site-shots.mjs ). The test build still reads services and files outside its config dir (the classifier socket, the dispatcher, state_dir ). For recordings, point GITOODO_STATE_DIR , GITOODO_CONFIG_DIR and GITOODO_BIN_DIR at an empty temporary folder so nothing of an installed Gitoodo shows up or is touched. A real test repository beside the fixture For flows the fixture cannot show (a real clone, worktree and agent session, e.g. "Solve with an agent", #919), an account of the test config may reach its real forge: add it to settings.json of the test config dir and hand its token to the test app in the launch environment as GITOODO_TOKEN_<ID> (the id in upper case, other characters as _ , as for a headless service; docs/daemon.md ). Start the binary directly (not open --env ), so the token is not in an argument list. Such an account stays across starts and uses the real forge adapter; an account without the variable is removed as before, and the showcase never keeps one. The keychain is never read or written. Point GITOODO_STATE_DIR , GITOODO_LOG_DIR and GITOODO_BIN_DIR at a temporary folder, set the repository's local_path and dispatch.worktree_root in the test config's orchestration.json to that folder too, and run your own gitoodo classifier (and gitoodo dispatcher , with a stub agent first on PATH ) with the same variables and GITOODO_CONFIG_DIR set to the test config dir before the app starts: the test build shares the service labels with an installed release, so it would otherwise ask the release's services. Use a dedicated test repository only. Optional native navigation measurements (#337) Add VITE_TEST_PERFORMANCE=1 alongside VITE_TEST_ACCESS=1 to the build command. Both build flags are required; the dynamically imported probe is excluded from normal builds. Runtime automation alone does not enable it. Launch the scale fixture as above. Before the actual run, calibrate accessibility visibility in the real test app: use agent-desktop snapshot --app "Gitoodo Test" --max-depth 50 and reconstruct the readonly report fields as described below, then perform one native input and read them after a quiet pause. If the platform omits this offscreen field or its value, the measurement is not validated. Restart the test process after calibration; only a fresh process resets it. The probe counts trusted keydown , pointerdown , wheel and actual scroll events. Scroll includes browser-generated scroll events, including programmatic scrolling; trust alone does not prove a human caused a scroll. Non-trusted events and non-finite, zero, negative or future timestamps are rejected. Timestamps must share the performance.now() time origin. It records event timestamp to next animation callback scheduling latency , and gaps between animation callbacks during an input/scroll burst and its 250 ms quiet tail. These are neither pixel-paint/full-response latency nor displayed FPS. A delayed callback can extend that tail; no idle loop runs afterward. Use a foreground, visible window and record the native actions, dataset and environment with the result. No pass/fail threshold is inferred from these numbers. Read the fields only after the burst is quiet: reporting updates values and creates any additional fragment fields after sampling stops, without live announcements, focus changes or page layout changes. The JSON contains accepted counts by event type, rejected counts, pending queue overflow, burst count, elapsed process window and accumulated active window in milliseconds. eventToNextRafSchedulingMs and frameGapMs each include observed/retained/dropped counts and nearest-rank p50/p95/max of the first 4,096 retained samples (zero when empty). Pending event timestamps also cap at 4,096; overflow events are counted but not measured. Results are cumulative until process exit. No targets, key values, content, account data, network requests or logs are collected. The probe adds measurement overhead; corroborate the numbers with native navigation observations, rather than treating them as paint proof. The accessibility helper caps individual values at 120 characters. Read the header test-performance and test-performance-part-0 through parts - 1 using a full snapshot (without -i ). Each part is sequence:index:fragment with at most 96 characters of JSON. Require every sequence to match the header, join fragments by index and check the header character count before parsing. Discard mixed or incomplete reads; do not focus the fields to read them. The report is published only after a quiet burst. The installed store preview (#235) The signed, sandboxed store preview has no test build features, but it has one runtime switch: start it with GITOODO_UI_AUTOMATION=1 in its environment. Without the variable nothing differs from a normal start (no visible change, no permission prompt). osascript -e 'quit app "Gitoodo"' # single instance: a running app ignores the variable open -n --env GITOODO_UI_AUTOMATION=1 /Applications/Gitoodo.app "${GITOODO_AGENT_DESKTOP:-agent-desktop}" find --app Gitoodo --native-id shell-root --first With the switch on, the app is a regular (Dock) app so the accessibility API lists it, the real borderless popover opens at start (no tray click) and

t: Privacy policy: feedback and usage statistics
b: Single source for the privacy policy text of the app and the website (sections "Feedback" and "Usage statistics"). All outgoing connections of the app are listed in privacy-network-inventory.md . Publisher and controller: the GbR behind Gitoodo (contact: the GbR mailbox named in the imprint). Rationale for the feedback rules: Microsoft Store policy 10.5.2 (data is shared only after opt-in). The usage statistics are on by default by the maintainer's decision of 2026-11-16, in every build. Principle Feedback is submitted only when you press Send . Nothing is published, and there are no automatic feedback prompts. After you submit, queued messages are retried automatically for up to 24 hours. Store builds may show the system's own rating request now and then; Settings → System turns it off or stops it for good. Sending is opt-in per message ; nothing you chose for one message carries over to the next. What is sent Data When Your text and the category Always, because it is the message itself Technical details Only if you tick it for this message (preview shown) Logs Only if you tick it for this message (preview shown) Screenshots Only if you attach them for this message (preview shown) Reply address Only if you enter one; off by default App version Always, so we know which build the message is about Message ID Always; random per message, lets retries arrive only once Tokens, hosts and accounts are never sent. You see a preview of exactly what will be sent before you press Send. Path and processors The app sends the message to the GbR's own relay. The relay sits behind Cloudflare (traffic passes Cloudflare's network). The relay forwards it by email to the GbR mailbox. Processors: Cloudflare, the mail provider the relay uses to send, and the mail provider hosting the recipient mailbox (GbR). Log and retention The relay stores no message content. It logs only metadata: sender ID (public application ID), time, reference ID, result, size and a daily-salted IP hash (not reversible, changes every day). Metadata is deleted after 14 days . For abuse protection and safe retries it also keeps, for at most 24 hours, rate-limit counters per salted IP hash and the message ID with its reference. The received email stays in the GbR mailbox until the matter is handled and is used only to answer you and improve Gitoodo. The app keeps an unsent draft on your device. After you submit a message, temporary delivery failures place that message and its selected details in the local outbox. Retries stop after 24 hours. Finished outbox entries are removed after seven days while the app is running; when the app is closed, cleanup happens on its next start. The editable draft remains until successful delivery or until you clear it. Reply contact A reply address is optional and off by default. Without it we cannot answer you. It is used only to reply to this message. Website contact form The website ( site/ , privacy page section "Contact form") has its own form on the same relay, with the browser sender gitoodo-web ( gitoodo-web-test for local previews). Only when the visitor presses Send does the browser post the message, the chosen category, the reply address if entered, and the page's language and path (no query) to relay.silvio-und-maik.de ; nothing else, no technical details, logs or screenshots. Path, processors, log and retention are the same as above, except that the logged sender ID is the fixed website sender, not an installation ID. To block abuse the relay counts requests per HMAC-hashed IP address for one hour. In the browser the form stores only the flag gitoodo.site.contact.greeted (greeting seen or closed) in localStorage; the draft lives in memory while the page is open. Without JavaScript or if the relay is unreachable, the page offers the GbR mailbox instead. Your rights Access, correction, deletion, restriction, objection and complaint to a supervisory authority under GDPR. Write to the GbR mailbox and quote the reference ID shown after sending. Usage statistics Gitoodo can send anonymous usage statistics so we can see how the app is used and improve it for the people who use it. The statistics are on by default , and you can switch them off at any time. Default and switching off The last onboarding step shows the switch "Help make Gitoodo better", on by default, with what is sent and what never is. You can switch it off right there; "Finish" stores your choice. Settings → General has the same switch at any time. Nothing is sent before "Finish" stores the choice. Installs without a stored choice (installs that finished onboarding before this feature, or an onboarding that was closed early) send nothing, and Settings → General shows the switch off for them; they are not switched on silently. Running the introduction again from Help shows the switch on and stores it at "Finish". Running the introduction again shows the stored choice; it never resets it to the default. The setup steps you go through before the last step are held in memory only . When "Finish" stores "on" they are sent with their original times; when it stores "off", or when the app quits first, they are dropped. Switching off (on the last onboarding step or in Settings → General) stops sending at once (a request on its way is cancelled), deletes the install ID and drops everything still queued. Switching on again starts with a new install ID. The choice is stored per installation in usage.json in the app's config folder. It is not part of the settings export, import or backup. What is measured Only fixed identifiers from one list in the code ( crates/core/src/usage/taxonomy.rs ), never free text. A test checks every possible event against a parameter whitelist. Onboarding: which step was shown, left with next, skip or back, or closed (step name only); the token wizard page and the token check result per forge type; the error kind when a repo list could not load; which setup parts were done, skipped or failed. Use: which views, help entries and help center topics are opened; whether the introduction tour was finished or skipped and the weekly review was dismissed or switched off; that a question was forwarded (never to whom); slash command names of Gitoodo's own commands (an agent's commands count only as "agent"); answers by kind (card or comment, with or without AI help); the result of the system check; error kinds of failed commands and background services; counts of chat messages, started workers and merged pull requests. Milestones, once per install: first question seen, first answer sent, first worker started, first pull request merged, first chat message. An app start event and one "alive" event per day. Context of each visit: app version, build variant (direct macOS, Mac App Store, Windows installer, Microsoft Store, Linux), operating system and architecture, mode (direct or orchestrator), UI language, the forge types in use (Forgejo, Gitea, GitHub, GitLab), whether they are cloud hosts, self-hosted or both, the orchestrator agent type, the number of accounts and enabled repos as a range (for example "6-20"), the install week and the install age as a range of days. Pages are synthetic addresses such as app://gitoodo/board ; no referrer is sent. What is never measured Contents of issues, pull requests, comments, answers, questions or chats. Names of repos, accounts, organisations, labels, branches or people. Tokens, passwords, keys or webhook addresses. Addresses of your forge servers or other hosts (only "cloud", "self-hosted" or "mixed"). Free text of any kind, including error messages (only the error kind). Install ID A random 16-digit hexadecimal ID is created when the choice "on" is stored ("Finish" with the switch on, or switching it on in Settings) and links the events of this installation. It is stored only in usage.json , is deleted when you switch the statistics off and is replaced by a new one when you switch them on again. It is not derived from the device, the account or any other identifier, and it is a different ID from the sender ID of the feedback relay: the two cannot be joined. Forgejo check Forgejo and Gitea share one API. To tell them apart for the forge type, Gitoodo asks each self-hosted Gitea-type server once, without a token, for /api/forgejo/v1/version and keeps only the answer "Forgejo" or "Gitea". This happens only while the statistics are on; the server address itself is never sent to the statistics server. Path, processing and retention Events go in batches, at the latest every 15 minutes, by HTTPS to the GbR's own Matomo instance at matomo.silvio-und-maik.de (server in the EU). No third party receives them. Offline, up to 500 events wait locally in usage.json ; events older than 23 hours are dropped instead of being sent late. The app sets no cookies. Matomo stores IP addresses only shortened (IPv4 by two bytes, IPv6 correspondingly); the full address is used only while the request is processed, for the country lookup. Raw visit data is deleted on the Matomo instance after 180 days ; only aggregated reports remain. Because the install ID is random and deleted when you switch the statistics off, switching off ends any link between future and past events. Builds without a statistics site ID (development builds, forks), the test access build, UI automation runs and the browser demo record and send nothing. Your rights for the statistics Switching off in Settings → General ends all sending. Access, deletion and objection under GDPR: write to the GbR mailbox.
