Gitoodo can report new questions to a chat through an outgoing webhook (Slack, Teams, or Matrix/generic). It is off by default. Settings: type, webhook URL, on/off, "send question text", "daily digest", the login-to-handle mapping for mentions, and "send test message". Secret handling The webhook URL is a secret. It lives only in the keychain (service gitoodo , key chat-webhook ), never in the settings file, an export, a log line or an error text. The frontend can only ask "configured yes/no"; the URL is write-only. Failures are reported as a category ( invalid , not_configured , unreachable , timeout , tls , status , keychain ) and logged with the host only. All network access is in crates/core/src/chat . Message Repo, title, deadline and a link to the issue. The question text is added only with the option "send question text" (default off) and is cut at 500 characters. Payload per type: Type Body Slack {"text": ...} (mrkdwn) Teams message with one Adaptive Card 1.4 attachment Matrix / generic {"text": ..., "html": ...} (plain text and escaped HTML, for hooks) Mentions A message mentions the person asked: the login in the header of the question's first addressed block, or the new person of a forward. The settings map forge logins to chat handles; the mapping is not a secret and lives in the settings file ( chat.handles ). Logins match in any case. A login without a usable handle gets no mention. A handle must not contain blanks, control characters or < > & " | , and is at most 128 characters; at most 200 mappings are kept. Type Handle Written as Slack member ID U… / W… , user group ID S… <@U…> , <!subteam^S…> ; anything else as plain @handle Teams sign-in address (UPN) or Entra object ID <at>handle</at> plus a mention entity in msteams Matrix user ID @user:server link pill to https://matrix.to/#/@user:server ; else text Forwards Forwarding a question (see docs/question-format.md , "Forwarding") sends one message "Question forwarded: <title>" with repo, link and the mention of the new person, never the question text. It counts against the same hourly limit; in digest mode it becomes a digest line. Daily digest With "daily digest" (default off) new questions are not sent one by one. They are queued in chat-notified.json and sent as one message once a day has passed since the first queued item: a title with the count, then one line per question with title, repo, link and mention (at most 20 lines, then "+N"). The digest never carries the question text. The queue survives a restart; the rules below (once per question, no replay, hourly limit) still apply. Delivery rules At most once per question: a question is marked as reported before it is sent and the mark is persisted ( chat-notified.json ), so a restart never repeats it. A failed send is not repeated. No replay: a question waiting longer than 1 hour is marked as reported without sending. This covers offline gaps, the first poll after a restart and the moment the feature is enabled. Such questions are dropped, not caught up. Bursts: per poll at most 3 single messages; the rest is one summary message ("N more questions"). Rate limit: at most 20 messages per hour, 1 s between messages; the excess is dropped and logged. Errors: exactly one attempt, no retry. After a failure the rest of that batch is dropped. The warning is throttled. Removing an account forgets its marks and its queued digest lines.

Gitoodo asks, rarely and quietly, whether someone wants to support its development. Supporting unlocks nothing; every feature works the same without it. The wording is "Unterstützen" / "support", never "Spende" / "donation" (the publisher is not a charity and issues no receipts). Where Settings : the row "Entwicklung unterstützen" with a pink heart ( settings-support ) opens the support page. It is always there, also after "Nicht mehr fragen". Footer heart ( footer-support ): a small pink heart at the trailing end of the status footer, in every view, opens the same page; label and tooltip "Entwicklung unterstützen". It is permanent and quiet (no badge, no counter, no animation) and does not count as an ask: the rules below stay unchanged. Inline ask ( support-ask ): a card above the tab list after an answer was sent from the detail view, i.e. at the place of the success. No dialog, no focus move, nothing blocked. Its three actions: open the page ( support-ask-open ), "Später" ( support-ask-later ), "Nicht mehr fragen" ( support-ask-never ). Weekly review ( weekly-review-ask , #707): when the ask is due, the weekly review card (see below) may carry it instead, with the same three actions and the same wording; without payment links (Mac App Store or unknown channel) the text names only a star or a recommendation. When the card shows Rules live in src/views/support/logic.ts (pure functions, tested with simulated time). Rule Value Earliest ask next success after 3 successes Successes spread over at least 2 different local days Asks per installation, at most 3 Pause after showing or "Später" 90 days Pause after opening a payment link 270 days "Nicht mehr fragen" final, no further asks A success is an answer sent successfully from the detail view. Showing the card already counts as an ask and starts the 90-day pause, so a card closed by navigating away is not shown again on the next answer. Pauses only ever grow, never shorten. A payment click is never treated as a payment; the app does not know and does not track whether anyone paid. One prompt per session, shared cap (#707, #712). The inline ask, the weekly review and the store rating request share one cap, kept by the Rust core ( crates/core/src/asks.rs , ledger in asks.json ): at most one prompt per app session, and at least 14 days between two asks in both directions. Whichever claims it first is the only prompt until the next start. The inline card claims the cap through claim_support_ask , and only when its own rules ( askAllowed ) already allow an ask; with a closed cap the success still counts but no card shows. The weekly review claims it through claim_review ( offerReview in src/views/support/logic.ts ). It always takes the session's one prompt. It carries the ask only when reviewAsk allows it (the same askAllowed limits) and 14 days have passed since the last ask; then it counts as a support ask in the shared cap and is recorded with recordAsk (one ask, 90-day pause), exactly like the inline card. A review without the ask does not start the 14-day spacing, otherwise the weekly card would hold every other ask. Answers to the card ("Später", "Nicht mehr fragen", a payment link) only change support.json ; they never reach the cap or the rating state (no review gating). The thresholds are a hypothesis for this app: answering questions is rarer than the operations other apps count, so "3 answers over 2 days" stands for experienced use. Revisit them if the card turns out to come too early or never. Weekly review Once a week a calm card ( weekly-review ) appears above the list: answered questions, median answer time, merged pull requests and closed issues of the last 7 days, computed on the device from the user's own forge data ( loop_metrics , see docs/metrics.md ). Rules live in src/views/review/model.ts (pure, tested): On by default; "Wochenrückblick" in Settings → Notifications ( settings-weekly-review ) or "Wochenrückblick ausschalten" on the card switches it off ( weekly_review in settings.json ). The first start only remembers the current week; the first review comes the week after. The week starts on the region's first weekday. The week it was offered in is kept in localStorage ( gitoodo.weeklyReview.week ); "Schließen" ends it for that week. A week without answers, merges or closed issues shows nothing and counts as done. When another prompt already showed in this session, the review waits for a later session of the same week. Channels (fail-closed) supportChannel() maps the build variant ( build_variant command) to a channel; supportWays() decides what the page shows. Channel Payment links Star and share Direct download (macOS outside the App Store) PayPal, Ko-fi, GitHub Sponsors; Buy Me a Coffee behind "Weitere Wege" yes Windows installer and Microsoft Store (MSIX) same as direct (Microsoft Store Policy 10.8.2 allows third-party payments) yes Mac App Store none, and no mention of them in any text (Guideline 3.1.1) yes Any other OS, unknown build, or still loading none yes Addresses The default payment addresses live in one file, src/views/support/destinations.ts ; the app reads them through src/views/support/links.ts , and the project URL is shared with the About section. The landing page imports the same file and the app's support texts ( src/i18n/support.ts and its locales) in every site language. GitHub's "Sponsor" button ( .github/FUNDING.yml ) and the README's "Support" section cannot import it; tests/support-links.test.ts fails when either drifts from it. A distributor can replace or clear each payment address at build time: VITE_SUPPORT_PAYPAL_URL , VITE_SUPPORT_KOFI_URL , VITE_SUPPORT_GITHUB_URL , VITE_SUPPORT_BMAC_URL . An empty value or anything that is not https:// counts as missing: the way is hidden and the page names what is missing ( support-missing ). The project has no NETWORK.md . The support feature adds these external addresses; they are only opened in the external browser on a click, never fetched by the app: https://www.paypal.com/donate/… https://ko-fi.com/silviol https://github.com/sponsors/silvio-l https://buymeacoffee.com/silvio.lindstedt the project URL (star) Provider logos are local SVGs in src/assets/support/ (origin and licence in its README); no hotlinking, no third-party scripts or widgets. Storage The ask state (successes, days, asks, pause, declined) is stored by the Rust core in support.json in the app data directory ( crates/core/src/store/support.rs ), read leniently and written atomically. The shared ask cap lives in asks.json ( crates/core/src/store/asks.rs ). Neither file is part of the settings export, and neither is part of the usage statistics ( docs/privacy.md ). There is no payment code.
